But now Garrett is back, and he said he and Donald playing together can give the Rams an “elite defense” for the rest of the season.

#2857. LeBron James has become the king without a home

CLEVELAND — The opposite of love isn't hate, it's apathy.

LeBron James has gotten many receptions from Cleveland Cavaliers fans over his 24 seasons in the league. None have been as half-hearted and uncarring as Friday's.

There's always been a certain buzz in the arena when James plays in Cleveland. That has been the case since he was in high school.

That juice, however, was lacking in his first trip back home in a Philadelphia 76ers uniform. There were empty seats before tip-off. The ovation for him when he was announced in the starting lineups was positive, but hardly more than respectful. No tribute video was played, as has been the case for the last eight seasons. There were smatterings of boos and cheers throughout the night, but nothing more than what any other high-profile player gets at Rocket Arena. And a good number of fans were content heading out while James was still on the court.

In short, LeBron was just another guy participating in one of 41 home games against the Cavs.

"At this point it's become normal," Donovan Mitchell said of James's return. "My first year, you see it, and now it's just, we're playing the Sixers, to be honest. You obviously understand that the stands are going to be packed and obviously cheer for him, and rightfully so. He's a champion, he's from here, and he deserves all that and more for what he's done for the city. At this point it's just regular. … For us it's normal."

The normality of this reception stands in stark contrast to what we saw last year. Then, the crowd showered him with praise all game, ultimately moving him to tears. At the time, it seemed unfathomable that he would receive anything but love in the building he called home for 11 years. This summer, however, changed that.

James chose to leave the Los Angeles Lakers in free agency at the end of June. He then spent the first three weeks in July dragging his feet, leading those within the city and organization to believe he was returning to Cleveland. But then James threw a curveball and decided to go to a city he had no previous connection with and build a super team with the 76ers.

LeBron has earned the right to ring chase at the age of 41. But that comes with consequences, especially when you choose a conference rival over returning to a good team back home that also has a chance of winning a championship.

We saw the fallout of that choice on Friday night. There wasn't the pain and vitriol from 2010. There wasn't the love in all of his returns since 2018. Just emptiness.

LeBron understandably preferred this reaction to what he got when he first returned as a member of the Miami Heat. "Nothing can get as worse as December 2, 2010, from a reception standpoint," James said. "I've seen the end of the depths of hell when it comes to a reception here."

That night in 2010 was an absolute disaster. Cleveland should've handled that moment better. They have deserved all of the blame and condemnation that has come from how they handled that. Yet, hate comes from a place of passion. It comes from pain, an emotion that's real. Fans cared about what happened that night.

On Friday, I'm not sure if anyone cared too much anymore. There was appreciation, but there wasn't undying love. There was frustration, but not enough to actually voice that displeasure. Just a tiredness of a decades-long relationship that keeps oscillating back and forth, without either side really being sure how much they mean to the other.

That uncarrying is the saddest place a relationship can find itself, especially one as personal as this. Arguably no professional athlete has meant more to a region than LeBron to Northeast Ohio. The journey from being the teenage prodigy from Akron to delivering the first professional championship in over half a century for a sports-starved region is truly impossible to put into words.

The relationship between LeBron and northeast Ohio will continue in some form beyond this. Maybe that appreciation is there if he plays future games in Cleveland. And most likely, that outpouring of love will return for the inevitable statue and jersey retirement ceremonies.

But then again, that isn't guaranteed. James's choice to presumably end his career in a different uniform could just be the straw that broke the camel's back. The rift that caused both sides to continue drifting apart forever.

Friday could have been LeBron's last professional game in Northeast Ohio. Nothing about the future is guaranteed. And if so, there couldn't have been a more pitiful way for things to end in Cleveland.

#2856. After career-low numbers in 2025, Justin Jefferson's production is even lower in 2026

Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson had his worst season in 2025. When a great player like Jefferson has an off year, the hope is that he’ll bounce back the next year. That hasn’t happened.

Jefferson’s stats are actually worse across the board in 2026 than they were in 2025, when he seemed to have reached the bottom of what a player his caliber is capable of producing.

Last year, Jefferson finished with a career-low 1,048 receiving yards. This year, heading into Week 9, Jefferson has just 335 receiving yards.

Last year, Jefferson averaged a career-low 12.5 yards per catch. This year, Jefferson is averaging 12.0 yards per catch.

Last year, Jefferson had a career-low 47 receiving first downs. This year, Jefferson has 17 receiving first downs.

Last year, Jefferson averaged a career-low 4.9 catches per game. This year, Jefferson is averaging 4.7 catches per game.

Last year, Jefferson averaged a career-low 61.6 receiving yards per game. This year, Jefferson is averaging 55.8 yards per game.

The major question to ask is whether this means Jefferson has declined, or whether the blame goes to the Vikings’ quarterbacks who haven’t been able to get him the ball over the last two years. An answer to that question may come on Monday night against the Bills, when Carson Wentz starts in place of Kyler Murray, who has been announced as out with a hamstring injury.

Jefferson’s best game this year came in Week 1, when he had just two catches for 11 yards early on with Murray in the game, then caught six passes for 81 yards and two touchdowns from Wentz after Murray left with a concussion. Jefferson also had his best games last year catching passes from Wentz: Jefferson averaged 95.4 yards per game in the five games Wentz started in 2025, and averaged just 47.6 yards per game in the 12 games started by J.J. McCarthy and Max Brosmer.

If Wentz and Jefferson connect for a big game on Monday night, it may spur Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell to decide Wentz is his quarterback going forward. If Wentz can’t get the most out of Jefferson’s playmaking abilities on Monday night, the Vikings may decide on Tuesday morning that it’s time to go shopping for a new quarterback at the trade deadline.

#2855. Report: Colts are in trade talks regarding QB Daniel Jones

The Indianapolis fire sale could indeed extend to the man who was supposed to become a franchise quarterback there.

According to ESPNFL, the Colts have engaged in trade talks this week regarding Daniel Jones, speaking to “multiple teams.”

The precise language of the report identifies only one team as actually talking to the Colts. From the article, the Ravens “were one team to check in on Jones.” The Ravens ultimately struck a deal with the Cardinals for quarterback Jacoby Brissett, whose plunge from No. 1 to No. 3 on the depth chart made it clear to the rest of the league that he was available.

The only other team mentioned by name is the Vikings, and the report points only to "[s]peculation” involving Minnesota. (We’ve been “speculating” about it since the immediate aftermath of Sunday’s loss by the Vikings in Detroit.)

Past ESPNFL reporting on a potential trade for running back Jonathan Taylor ultimately listed five teams as talking to the Colts (Giants, Seahawks, Broncos, Packers, Vikings). The fact that other teams weren’t mentioned as to Jones suggests that, frankly, there may not be other teams.

Really, which current contender would want him? The Vikings are the only potential playoff team that checks the box as possibly needing a starter right now. And only the Vikings and Giants are contenders with which Jones has direct experience. (The Giants wouldn’t want a Jones reunion, and Jones surely wouldn’t want it, either.)

That could change this weekend, obviously. One injury to a starter could alter the dynamics, spurring another contender to pick up the phone and make a push for Jones. The most memorable example of that came 15 years ago, when a broken collarbone to Raiders quarterback Jason Campbell prompted a quick deal for Bengals quarterback Carson Palmer, who had decided he didn’t want to play for the team that had drafted him — and who had yet to report.

Three years ago, Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins popped an Achilles tendon two days before the deadline, forcing the Vikings to scramble at the deadline to do a deal with the Cardinals for quarterback Josh Dobbs.

Absent a multi-week injury to a starting quarterback on a contender that doesn’t believe its backup can hold down the fort, the Vikings may be the only team that wants Jones at the deadline.

The preferences of Daniel Jones become a factor, too. If (as we firmly believe) he’s not happy that the Colts folded the tents by trading guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner after a 2-5 start that included an overtime loss to the Chiefs and a toe-to-toe battle with the then-unbeaten Vikings, Jones would have a clear interest in hopping to a contender.

The Vikings wanted to keep Jones after the 2024 season. He opted to sign with the Colts in part because he saw a more realistic path to winning the job over 2023 first-rounder Anthony Richardson in Indianapolis than 2024 first-rounder J.J. McCarthy in Minneapolis. If he’s told that a return to Minnesota would include being installed immediately as QB1, he’d surely prefer that to a lost season with the Colts.

Andd Jones has power over this process. Beyond the basic reality that no team wants a starting quarterback who doesn’t want to play for it, the 2027 roster bonus and base salary that become fully guaranteed in March ($10.51 million) are currently guaranteed for injury. The ESPNFL article mentions that Jones could waive the injury guarantee in order to expedite a deal.

The reverse of that (Jones refusing to waive the injury guarantee) means that Jones could block a trade, if avoiding a potential eight-figure guarantee for 2027 is a dealbreaker for his prospective employer.

Our guess? Right now, only the Vikings currently have interest in Jones. And a trade for Jones becomes a very viable possibility if the Vikings lose to the Bills on Monday with Carson Wentz playing quarterback.

Given the possibility that another team will emerge as a competitor to get Jones, it’s also possible that the Vikings have already decided to trade for Jones after Monday night’s game — win or lose — and that the two teams have agreed to keep it under wraps until Week 9 ends.

Either way, if the oft-injured Jones plays on Sunday against the Cowboys and gets injured, that would kill any chance to trade him. That makes it important to monitor Sunday’s game carefully. If the Colts apply a quick hook to Jones, it could mean that he’s already gone.

Lando Norris conquered thunderstorms to claim pole for the São Paulo Grand Prix while Lewis Hamilton suffered an engine nightmare and will be forced to start Sunday's race from the back of the grid.

In treacherous conditions at Interlagos, McLaren's Norris rose to the top as he pipped compatriot George Russell on the track – but the Mercedes man will start seventh after a five-place grid drop.

Kimi Antonelli, who deposed Norris as world champion last weekend, will be promoted to second while Liam Lawson – whose Racing Bulls seat remains in serious doubt – is a remarkable third on the grid.

Russell was again furious with his Mercedes team, questioning why they asked him to back off on his final flying lap – believing that decision cost him pole.

Ferrari announced ahead of final practice that both of their warring drivers would take 10-place grid drops, with Hamilton and Leclerc changing their internal combustion engine to incur the penalty.

But Hamilton immediately hit trouble. First he complained of vibrations from his new engine before having to come in again with his car pouring smoke from the back.

Ferrari subsequently decided that his entire power unit needed replacing, meaning the 41-year-old will need a miracle on Sunday.

Hamilton will be joined at the back of the pack by Max Verstappen, with the pair changing several engine components. Leclerc will line up 14th after his own penalty, leaving a scrambled order for what is expected to be a wet race.

Thunderstorms hit the track in the moments after final practice and it poured down again as qualifying began.

Some cars were in the pit lane when rain started and they tiptoed round before the session was swiftly red-flagged. Red Bull's Isack Hadjar was on the radio to ask for a new race suit, having been drenched.

"I'm so wet!" added the new world champion Kimi Antonelli. The 20-year-old remained in his car as the delay ticked past an hour.

Safety car driver Bernd Maylander did exploratory laps of the track, reporting back that it was "not driveable" as the weather worsened – with thunder bellowing over Interlagos.

Thoughts swiftly turned to this race in 2024, where qualifying was postponed until early Sunday morning.

"Definitely the wettest conditions I've experienced in a race car, in a car full stop I think!" Haas' Ollie Bearman said. "That's a lot for someone growing up in the UK."

Despite rain continuing to fall and the track still soaked, the FIA confirmed a restart for 4.26pm local time – an hour and 24 minutes after the red flag.

As the cars sat in the pits, the rain intensified again but the action resumed as Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas led the grid into the unknown on the lesser-used extreme wet tyre.

Home favourites Gabriel Bortoleto and Rafael Camara both banged the barriers – the latter remarkably continuing – but overall it was an extraordinary display by the drivers to keep their cars on track in appalling conditions.

Verstappen was third-fastest after Q1 but jumped out of his car to end his day early, knowing that he would start the race at the back regardless after a penalty for changing several engine components.

It is a position he is familiar with having done the same here over the last two years, famously winning from 17th in the rain in 2024.

Hamilton did not take the same approach as he began Q2 but when the grid switched to intermediates, the 41-year-old decided enough was enough and to save his tyres.

The second session came to an early halt when F1 debutant Camara drove into the barriers at Curva da Juncao, leaving McLaren's Oscar Piastri eliminated.

Russell was on the radio to say it was getting very dark on track as the day light disappeared.

Heavy rain fell again as the cars went out again but Norris showed his world champion quality, putting his car over a tenth clear of Russell.

The 28-year-old barked at his Mercedes engineer, believing he had been cost pole as his season of frustration continued.

"Congrats to Lando but that was a pole lap and a misjudgement on our side," Russell said.

#2842. Takeaways from a Celtics 3-point blitz in a buzzy win over the Hornets

Maybe it was because it was an NBA Cup game. Maybe it was because Jayson Tatum was visiting his old stomping grounds. Maybe it was because the Celtics caught fire from 3. Mix that all together with a few notable absences from the Hornets roster and we got a 119-80 Boston blowout at The Spectrum Center on Friday Night.

Before being drafted in 2023, Hornets' Brandon Miller called Paul George his GOAT. You can certainly see the similarities. The lanky 6'9 swingmen are both three level scorers with the biggest difference being the decade-plus between them.

Unfortunately, Miller left the game in the second half with a groin soreness with 8 points, a rebound, assist, steal, and block.

His idol put up similar numbers. Miller hit just 3-of-10; George was worse at 3-of-11.

However, the mutual admiration society doesn't end there. Tatum once posted back in 2015 when he was at Chaminade that he was "Baby PG" and even boasted that he thinks that he was the first college player to wear the PG1s at Duke.

And whenever the Celtics travel down to North Carolina, it's always going to be a special trip for Tatum. Even though The Hive is 150 miles away from Cameron Indoor Stadium, Tatum just has superpowers playing in Charlotte. Out of the 29 other NBA teams, Tatum averages the most points against the Hornets at nearly 30 per game. And in an NBA Cup game where point differential matters, the defending Player of the Week scored 34 points in just 29 minutes. He was 11-for-11 from the free throw line and 5-of-8 from behind the arc and neared triple-double territory with eight rebounds and nine assists without playing a minute in the fourth quarter.

The Celtics flirted with the NBA record for most threes in a game at 29, a feat they tied on Opening Night in 2024 against the Knicks. Boston had 17 at halftime and had it not been a blowout, they might have hit at least five more.

Instead, they settled for the NBA Cup record at 24 (on 44 attempts).

Up the eastern seaboard, the Maine Celtics opened their G League season against the Westchester Knicks in blowout fashion as well 123-94. Rookie Dillon Mitchell had six dunks and a triple, including this alley-oop from Milos Uzan.

Uzan and Chris Cenac Jr. had 21 a piece in the win.

"Just trying to channel my anger into love." — head coach Joe Mazzulla to CelticsBlog's Noa Dalzell on his mid-game hug with Neemias Queta

Mazzulla called a timeout because Queta fell down (again) and instead of just yelling at him, he gave him a hug.

After two games, the Celtics are 2-0 with a +53 differential. After the Hawks beat the Wizards 139-132 on Friday night, Boston stands alone at the top of the Eastern Conference's Group C. They'll continue this leg of their road-heavy November with a stop in Milwaukee on Sunday and then the marquee face-melter on Tuesday against the 76ers.

#2840. Beating Kyle Shanahan would be quite the feather in Klint Kubiak’s cap

Want to a crystal clear example of the kind of football team Klint Kubiak wants his Las Vegas Raiders to become?

Eye the San Francisco 49ers very closely this Sunday.

Because when Kubiak's Raiders head to Santa Clara to go toe-to-to with Shanahan's Niners, you'll get a bird's eye view a San Francisco team that plays complementary football and is 6-1 overall because of it. There have been fleeting moments of this for Las Vegas, however, the inability to harness consistency is a big reason why the team is 4-4 overall.

Curious as to why Shanahan's football team is one to model for Kubiak?

The pair of head coaches are steeped in the game, thanks to the coaching connection between their fathers Mike Shanahan and Gary Kubiak. The Kyle and Klint dynamic goes back to 1994 when Mike was the offensive coordinator and Gary the quarterbacks coach of the 49ers Super Bowl-winning coaching staff. The elder Shanahan and Kubiak continued to be tied at the hip with the Denver Broncos.

"Not a first one. Just really fortunate to grow up in that environment," Klint Kubiak said on a first memory he had with Kyle Shanahan with their dads coaching together. "I didn't know it at the time, but I got to be exposed to a lot of football at a young age, and I'm very grateful for that, myself and my brothers."

When Gary became the Houston Texans head coach, he gave Kyle his start as an offensive coordinator. And, in 2023, Kyle and Klint joined forces where the Kubiak was the passing game coordinator with the Shanahan dialing up the offense as head coach.

There's mutual respect and trust between the two families. And with a storied history together, similarities were bound to happen.

Foundationally, Shanahan's and Kubiak's respective offenses are deeply rooted in the same coaching tree. It's a philosophy designed to scheme play makers open with pre-snap motions and a balanced attack that showcases a physical and productive ground game. Specializing in the outside/wide-zone run scheme, the 49ers and Raiders eat off play action and the pre-snap motions both play callers habitually use not only identify and stress coverage schemes, but get pass catchers open.

Shanahan and Kubiak know to use running backs and tight ends in a variety of ways, so much so, that pass catching tailbacks and tight ends are often primary targets when the aerial attack is dialed up.

As the longstanding relationship between the two is undeniable, what's also without question is the two having their own distinct twist of the Shanahan-Kubiak offense.

Klint, for example, blended modern, rhythm-based passing concepts into the time-tested zone play-action tenets the system offers.

Taking into account the history between the two and the inherent competitiveness between them, beating Shanahan's 49ers this Sunday would be quite the feather in Kubiak's cap. Even now, there's another branch in the Shanahan-Kubiak dynamic as Klint's brother Klay is the 49ers offensive coordinator.

Like Shanahan, Kubiak won't be alone in his endeavor to coach his team past the 49ers and get his Raiders to back-to-back wins and a 5-4 record instead of a 4-5 mark.

Kubiak's chosen defensive coordinator — Rob Leonard — and special teams coordinator — Joe DeCamillis — must hold up their ends of the bargain in order to play complementary football against a really good 49ers team coming off its bye week. San Francisco is eyeing winning it's seventh game of the year as a proper bounce back from getting beat by the Atlanta Falcons 29-20 two Sunday's ago.

Las Vegas' defense will have its hand full stopping Shanahan and the fact Leonard's group is a cellar dweller statistically league-wise. Playing with much more discipline and urgency, alongside Leonard dialing up blitzes, is a must as the Raiders defense has allowed 30 or more points in the last five games.

"Well, I think if you've worked in the NFL long enough, then that's the reality of our business. It's a production business," Kubiak said of the confidence he has in Leonard. "It's the most competitive industry that I know of, and any time that you start to feel comfortable, then you will be quickly humbled. And so, whether you're having success or you're working to get better, if your mindset stays the same and you continue to push and push through the hard times, you come out on the other end. So, that's the NFL. The NFL brings adversity and makes you answer to it every day."

Offensively, Kubiak has veteran Kirk Cousins at quarterback producing 19 touchdown passes (second most int he league) to just five interceptions. Brock Bowers remains a reliable target for Cousins and is a difficult cover for cornerbacks and safeties, alike.

Cousins speaks highly of the 49ers defense led by Raheem Morris, a defensive coach that left an impression on the Raiders quarterback during their time together with the Washington Commanders.

"It's a great group. They're well coached. Fred Warner is one of the best linebackers in the league. (Nick) Bosa, Buck (DeForest Buckner), several of these guys are some of the best D-linemen in the league, and I think the secondary is also a very good group," Cousins said about Morris' 49ers defense. "They've made a lot of plays, so it's all three levels. You see the safeties really play hard, play fast. They'll strike you.

"So, it's a defense that played really well last year, playing really well this year. I feel like I've seen a lot of these same players and even somewhat the same scheme going back to when Kyle [Shanahan] first got there, and they've got a lot of continuity, and it shows in the tape."

#2838. Egypt sacks coach Hossam Hassan over 'negative impact' on team image

CAIRO (AP) — Egypt coach Hossam Hassan was sacked on Saturday for what the soccer federation cited as "a negative impact on the positive image of the team."

The Egyptian Football Association did not elaborate in a statement, adding only that "maintaining the team's stability is a paramount priority" that cannot be compromised.

Egyptian media believed the decision had more to do with Hassan's personal life than rumors of disagreements with Egypt players including star forward Mohamed Salah.

Egypt's Supreme Council for Media Regulation banned Hassan last week from appearing in all media outlets, an unprecedented decision against a national coach. That followed disputes in Hassan's personal life becoming public.

Hassan was appointed Egypt coach in 2024 and became the first former Egypt player to coach the national team at a World Cup this year. Egypt was knocked out by Argentina in the last 16.

The EFA immediately replaced Hassan with Ali Maher, a long-time head coach in the Egyptian Premier League currently leading fourth-placed Ceramica Cleopatra.

Maher must get quickly up to speed. Egypt plays Malawi on Nov. 13 and 17 in qualifying for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations. Egypt leads Group B.

#2837. Joe Burrow can become third quarterback with four or more TD passes in four straight games

Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow had seven touchdown passes in his team’s first four games of the season. In the last three, he has had 13.

Burrow currently leads the league with 20 touchdown passes. And the Bengals, after starting 2-2, are now 5-2.

They face the 3-5 Falcons on Sunday morning in Madrid at 9:30 a.m. ET on Sunday.

#2836. Game Preview: Knicks at Cavaliers, November 7, 2026

Some members from Generation Z might believe that the history of the Cleveland Cavaliers started and ended with a man named LeBron James (not once but twice). They couldn't be more wrong. The Cavs joined the NBA in 1970 and accumulated plenty of interesting anecdotes through the years, especially early on. For example, they scouted the players for their expansion Draft with the help of trading cards that assistant coach Jim Lessig discovered while shopping for a few gallons of milk.

On that understandably subpar inaugural roster was also a man named Gary Suiter, whose biggest contributions were eating hot dogs in the stands during warmups and calling the front office disguised as a fan, lobbying for more playing time for—you guessed it—Gary Suiter. When the well-known bachelor tried to shake down the Cavs for bigger travel expenses by hiring a prostitute to play his wife, even the desperate Cavaliers had enough and kicked him out.

Later on, though, basketball really took off in Ohio. The Cavs featured some really exciting teams, especially when the aforementioned James came to town and then came again to actually win a title. Other teams that are fondly remembered in "The Land" are the squads from the late 1980s and 1990s that featured stalwarts like Mark Price, Ron Harper, Brad Daugherty, or Craig Ehlo. Exactly: the guy who is mostly remembered for crumbling to the floor after Michael Jordan's famous first "shot", one of the most iconic images in league history.

How history and Cleveland will remember the current iteration of Cavaliers remains to be seen, yet it might very well be decided this year. The headliners on Kenny Atkinson's team are mostly unchanged from last year's Eastern Conference Finals sweep at the hands our Knickerbockers. That result could be described as another conquered mountain ledge on the Knicks' way to the NBA summit, or seen as just another failure by a Cavs' core that's been trying to win it all for about three years now.

At the heart of that core has been Donovan Mitchell and he is still the headliner at Rocket Arena this season. The stocky highflyer is scoring an efficient 22.5 points per game while probably sporting one of the more explosive games in the league these days. Fans are lamenting his decision making though, criticizing his constant hero ball and what they get for a massive $273 million dollar deal he signed in the summer. Next to Mitchell, a now 37-year-old James Harden runs the point for the Cavaliers, which might also impact "Spida" negatively. The former MVP is showing his age early on, only connects on 38 percent of his shots, and looks disinterested doing it every second night out.

Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen still form Cleveland's frontline—with all their shortcomings, yet also with plenty of talent. The ultra versatile Mobley has taken his physique and his game to another level in recent years, sports a much better jumper from the outside, and the former Defensive Player of the Year isn't moved off his spots as easily he used to be. If you want a big to switch effortlessly on Jalen Brunson, he's your man. His current season has been particularly promising with shooting splits of 56/48.6 (we'll ignore the 63 percent from the line this time around). Allen is kind of there: big, athletic, and skilled, yet you won't see him in any Strongman or Tough Mudder competitions any time soon.

Even if Cleveland got a bit longer and a bit more athletic, you still have to wonder where all of this is really going. They are good but how good really? Can they really compete with the top teams in the East? So far there is just a lot of "meh" in their profile. Standing at 5-4 they rank 9th in offensive rating and 14th in defensive rating. They play with a solid yet unspectacular pace (thank you, James Harden) and are average at best on the boards or from the field. Cleveland doesn't turn the ball over, which is good, yet doesn't force any turnovers either, which is bad (only the Bucks and Knicks make the opponent cough the ball up fewer times than Cleveland).

To be fair, Cleveland is a team that for the most part knows who it is, and such groups can take a little time shaking off the rust, especially after a long last season—we as Bocker buddies know all about it. The Cavaliers, just like the Knicks again, have a lot of things going for them, but it seems like Cleveland unlike New York also has a definitive ceiling. I'd mostly call it James Harden as he has never shown that he can be the ultimate difference maker in the postseason, at least not in a good way. Until then of course the Cavaliers are a perfectly fine, quality opponent, especially at home. They just proved it in their NBA cup last night against the Philadelphia 76ers, dismantling the fighting Nurses 119-95.

Let's hope our Knicks fare a little better tonight and that the biggest historical significance of this game is another win for the good guys. At the very least we don't have to worry about any of our players binge eating in the stands before the game, I guess. As funny as that would be.

#2835. Maryland's 2nd half turnaround leads to 34-29 win at Purdue to snap long losing streaks

WEST LAFAYETTE, Ind. (AP) — Malik Washington ran for two scores and threw for two more Saturday as Maryland overcame a sluggish first half to get its first win in nearly two months, 34-29 at Purdue.

The Terrapins (3-6, 1-5 Big Ten) snapped a six-game losing streak and a 13-game skid in conference play. It gave Aazaar Abdul-Rahim his first win since being named interim coach following the firing of Michael Locksley.

Washington was 13 of 18 for 253 yards with one interception. He also rushed eight times for 32 yards despite wearing a brace over his left knee in the second half. DeJuan Williams had 14 carries for 99 yards and scored on a 75-yard run. Chris Durr Jr. finished with four catches, 127 yards and a nifty 87-yard TD catch that essentially sealed the win.

Purdue (3-6, 2-4) has lost three straight. Ryan Browne was 24 of 38 for 296 yards and lost a fumble. Fame Ijeboi and Xavier Townsend each had a scoring run. But the Boilermakers had four red-zone trips end with field goals.

Washington wasted no time showing everyone how different the second half would be.

He capped the first possession of the third quarter by hooking up with Na'eem Abdul-Rahim Gladding on a short screen pass that Gladding took 44 yards for a score to give Maryland a 14-12 lead. Washington converted on the next series with 1-yard scoring plunge after Browne fumbled at the Boilermakers 2-yard line.

Purdue answered with Townsend's 30-yard TD run as the teams were still settling down from two shoving matches and three personal foul calls. That made it 21-19.

Williams' long run on the next offensive play made it 28-19.

A bad snap on third-and-goal inside the 1-yard line resulted in a 3-yard loss and forced the Boilermakers to settle for another field goal.

Then Durr caught a screen pass on second-and-19, broke multiple tackles as he raced all the way across the field and outran the defense for a TD to give Maryland a 34-22 cushion.

Purdue cut the deficit to 34-29 on Ijeboi's TD run and drove to Maryland's 11-yard line with 5 seconds to play. But Browne was sacked on the game's final play.

Maryland: The Terrapins lethargic offense produced just five first downs and 108 total yards in the first half, but whatever Abdul-Rahim said at halftime worked. They looked like a different team in the second half, hitting big play after big play in what may have been their last chance this season to end their Big Ten skid.

Purdue: The Boilermakers certainly will regret this loss. They settled for four field goals in the red zone and couldn't get the Terrapins stopped in the second half. A win would have put Purdue at .500 in league play — a solid step forward for second-year coach Barry Odom. Instead, they'll be trying to snap another losing streak next weekend.

Maryland defensive back Dontay Joyner took another twist Saturday when he was ejected for a flagrant personal foul just 96 seconds into the game. He got into it with a Purdue player on the game's second play. Three plays later, he was called for a shoving a player at the end of a play.

Purdue kicker Jacobo-Echeverria Lozano shattered the school's single-season record for a freshman with his first of five field goals Saturday. He made kicks from 47, 26, 24 and 36 yards to give the Boilermakers a 12-7 halftime lead. His 22-yard field goal in the second half gave him 21 this season — five more than the previous record.

Maryland: Hosts the Badgers next Saturday.

Purdue: Travels to No. 21 Iowa next Saturday.

The Raptors made Turner look like a child last night, which I was hoping wouldn't happen because Toronto was meant to be one of the trade suitors for him! Myles, this was your audition, SMH.

13 minutes, 4 points, 3 rebounds, 1 block, 2/7 FG, 0/4 3P, 0

Another rough game for Ware, who seemingly can't hit a three in a Bucks uniform, down to 20% on the year. Also not great to see him throw a fit on the sidelines after getting subbed off.

10 minutes, 3 points, 2 assists, 1 steal, 1 turnover, 1/2 FG, 0/1 3P, -9

Kind of a nothing-y game from Jakucionis. Again, he didn't do much wrong, but his niche of finding angles and getting into the lane looked harder against a gritty squad like the Raptors. KJ did make a great cut in the first half for his only field goal, though, which I loved.

38 minutes, 21 points, 11 rebounds, 6 assists, 1 block, 1 turnover, 8/14 FG, 1/5 3P, 4/6 FT, -5

Burries had his "I've arrived" game. I mean, we can talk about the scoring and athleticism around the rim, but I'm more interested in how he seems to grab every rebound in sight. It's surreal to watch. Grabbing six boards in the first quarter, Burries had this "I'm not losing tonight, so jump on my back" vibe about him. The kid just has this nose for the ball and a will to pursue it like very few players I've seen. Burries is showing he's a winner, and I can't wait for him to gain confidence from this game and give us more like it in the future.

24 minutes, 12 points, 1 block, 2 turnovers, 4/9 FG, 4/8 3P, -19

Whenever the Raptors looked like they were about to get the game out of reach, Green would hit a three. One thing I will always appreciate about Green is that, despite his unassuming nature, he is never scared of the moment. Hit two huge ones in the fourth.

15 minutes, 7 points, 1 block, 3/5 FG, -11

Ament got two of his three buckets in transition, while the other came on a nice baseline cut where he smartly waited for the defender to jump, then calmly put in the and-one. Not many other notes, other than that I thought Ament's minutes were generally quite positive.

Sims was forced into extended minutes because Turner had early foul trouble and Ware looked borderline unplayable at times. He did his job defensively, but you could tell the Raptors were happy to double all on-ball screens Sims set because they didn't trust his decision-making out of the short roll, which is a strategy we saw from opponents last year too.

Based on Jenkins's postgame comments, the team clearly wasn't doing much of what they had been instructed to do in practice. His decision to close with no centre was the right one, but that then made it tough to rebound. Part of the issue is that the Bucks are leaning on flawed veterans; you don't want to turn to Kuzma to close as a two-way wing, but there aren't many other great options, especially when you needed someone beefy enough to deal with Barrett. Jaquez is a fine player, but he's a seventh man on a good team. Turner is a great locker room guy, but he drives you mad with his lack of physicality. I say this to reiterate that Jenkins is working with a rough set of cards right now, and I struggle to think another coach could have got a different result with this same group of personnel.

DNP-CD: Ousmane Dieng, Caris LeVert, Gary Trent Jr.

Inactive: Kam Jones, Cormac Ryan, Pete Nance, Bogoljub Markovic,

Milwaukee's centre rotation might be the league's worst when both play poorly.

Jenkins was hot in his postgame presser, cutting off a reporter's question about what he saw from his struggling offence in the second half: "We were getting stops in the first half. We were playing fast. We didn't have to call sets. But then we just gave up second-chance opportunities, fouled them way too much, and they were taking the ball out of the net, so we couldn't play as fast as we needed to."

Jenkins also mentioned that the Bucks didn't "tag up," which means that when the shot goes up, all five players get to their man, which, when done right, impedes the opponent's ability to advance the ball up the floor and score in transition.

Jenkins said that after the game, Turner owned his bad performance to the group.

The broadcast showed a stat that over the last three games, Herro had scored 0 points in the first quarter and 62 in all other quarters. Crazy.

Speaking of Herro, I noticed he subbed back in earlier than usual in the fourth, which resulted in him breaking the ~30-minute pseudo-limit he had seemingly been operating under previously.

The Bucks return to Fiserv on Sunday night to face the Boston Celtics. Watch at 7:00 p.m. CST on MY24.

#2830. Maresca's dream start turns into nightmare as title hopes hit

Enzo Maresca left the City Ground on Saturday evening with chants of "can we play you every week?" ringing in his ears - and the Italian's dream start as Manchester City manager is rapidly turning into a nightmare.

Amid a sea of noise from the home faithful on the banks of the River Trent, the delirious Forest supporters witnessed their side produce a thrilling performance as City sunk to a third straight Premier League loss.

Maresca's leaky backline continues to make defensive blunders and once Josko Gvardiol gave the ball away for Jair Cunha to open the scoring in the sixth minute, City were on the back foot.

With Arsenal edging past Hull earlier in the day and keeping another clean sheet, City head into the international break searching for answers after a 3-1 loss and six points behind the champions.

Maresca said: "The first half we didn't match [Forest's] intensity or win duels or second balls. The first thing required in these games is intensity.

"We tried to react at 2-0 but it's too late. We scored one, probably could have scored more but in transition we concede one more. No panic. We need to understand but no panic."

Asked why the intensity was low, Maresca replied: "I need to analyse that."

The situation already looks bleak for City, but what does history show?

Should Brighton fail to beat Brentford on Sunday, Arsenal would be just the fourth side in Premier League history to have a six-point lead after 10 games, while only two teams have been so far behind as City at this stage and gone on to win the title.

One of those was Manchester United in 2002-03. The other? City themselves in 2013-14 under Manuel Pellegrini.

But Fabian Hurzeler's Brighton have the opportunity to leap up to second place and five points behind the Gunners should they beat Brentford.

There is another factor which looms large over City's campaign.

The club have lodged an appeal after being found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules.

That process is ongoing - and it is not yet known what potential sanctions City could face.

But - even if any possible punishment does not affect this season - their title hopes are looking slimmer by the match.

Delightful Delap and outfought Anderson - Forest v Man City player ratings

Has Anderson lived up to the hype after Man City move?

With his hands tucked inside his trouser pockets and his head bowed, a forlorn-looking Maresca paced the touchline towards the end of the match.

The City boss said during the week he was still getting to know his players, but performances like the one against Forest will provide some clarity as to who he can, and cannot, trust.

After starting the season with seven straight wins, City have hit real trouble with defeats against Aston Villa, Brighton and now a pumped-up Forest.

Their problems at the back are not helping as it was another game where individual errors cost them dearly - and former striker Liam Delap took full advantage of the lapses in concentration with two goals.

Gvardiol was at fault for the first, Iliman Ndiaye and Elliot Anderson got in a muddle for the second, while Matheus Nunes did not put a challenge in for the third.

"Before the game all the talk was about individual errors," former Forest winger Steve Stone told BBC Radio 5 Live. "Apart from the first goal, this hasn't been about that - the line is disjointed.

"The full-backs were very wide. If the ball turns over quickly and you pass it with your first pass you can be right through them. They have been exposed today.

"Oliver Glasner's team have played through them every time."

It was a miserable return to the City Ground for Anderson since his £116m move to City in the summer and the midfield dynamic alongside Enzo Fernandez does not seem to be working.

The Argentine should have scored with a headed chance from close range but spent much of the game complaining in referee Sam Barrott's ear - City team-mates and supporters may be expecting more from their club record signing.

The former Chelsea player scored in the midweek Champions League win at RB Leipzig, but that is his only goal or assist in his past nine games.

Maresca needs to work out how to get the best out of Fernandez during the international break.

Stone added: "I came here tonight thinking City would win, I thought they had chances. This is a real hammer blow to them, there is something not right about the back four at the minute.

"I have never seen a City team give the ball away so much in the middle of the park."

Rayan Cherki's stunning strike gave City hope but they could not turn it around and the numbers following the result make for grim:

City have lost three consecutive Premier League games for the first time since a run of four in November-December 2024

They have become the second team in English top-flight history - after Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05 - to win their first seven games of a season and then lose their next three

This was their first league defeat by two or more goals against a side starting the day in the relegation zone since November 2008 (a 2-0 loss to Bolton Wanderers).

Maresca was forced to chop and change his defence again, withdrawing both Gvardiol and Marc Guehi at half-time because of injuries, according to the manager.

It meant Nunes came in at right-back, with Abdukodir Khusanov moving inside, and Nico O'Reilly playing down the left.

Former Liverpool midfielder Danny Murphy told BBC Sport: "I thought City's performance was poor in terms of mentality.

"To make so make so many mistakes when you go anywhere in the Premier League, but especially to a team who are fighting for the lives, and you know they're going to come after you.

"They were sloppy with the ball, not winning duels. I would even probably go as far as saying there was probably a bit of arrogance at the start of the game from them.

"I think that there are now some big questions to ask the manager about how he gets them back on track. I think with the talent they have got, it is not going to be a big problem.

"But I think defensively, maybe sticking to the same backline for a little while is the way forward."

#2828. Jayson Tatum admits Charlotte ‘feels like home’ after NBA Cup masterclass

Despite being hundreds of miles away from Boston, Jayson Tatum had no trouble feeling at ease in Charlotte, North Carolina, on Friday night. For a moment, the Spectrum Center even began to sound like TD Garden.

Chants of 'Let's go Celtics' began filling the arena. In response, the Hornets began turning up the volume on their signature buzzing sound effect in an attempt to drown out the Celtics fans taking over Charlotte. It didn't work. When Tatum arrived at the free-throw line in the third quarter, he was greeted by a chorus of loud 'MVP' chants.

"It definitely feels like home," Tatum confessed after Boston's 119-80 NBA Cup win, per CLNS Media.

Tatum found his footing and began painting his latest masterpiece early on. He scored or assisted on 30 of the Celtics' first 40 first-quarter points, which tied Paul Pierce for the most 15-point first quarters (106) in the franchise's play-by-play history, according to ESPN Insights. By halftime, he had reached 24 points on 8-of-14 shooting, including 5-of-8 from beyond the arc, surpassing his combined 3-point makes from his three previous games.

If he wanted to, Tatum could've pursued his career-high (60 points). But instead, his night was called off after three quarters as the Celtics held a 96-57 runaway lead.

At that point, the damage was already done. Tatum only needed three frames to finish with 34 points, eight rebounds, and nine assists, falling a hair shy of securing his first triple-double of the season. He earned a fourth quarter of rest, watching from the bench as head coach Joe Mazzulla allowed reserves including Luka Garza, Mike Conley, and Ron Harper Jr. to get their reps in until the final buzzer.

The Celtics found a way to turn a trip to Charlotte into a home-away-from-home experience. For Tatum, as uplifting as the Boston fans in attendance may have been, the 28-year-old had other reasons to feel comfortable in North Carolina, dating back to his teenage years.

"I have a lot of connections here in this state, this area," he explained. "I came here as an 18-year-old kid, my first time spending real time away from home. I was here for a little under a year, and obviously the connection I have here with Duke and the relationships that I've been able to build. I always love coming back to North Carolina and love playing here. A lot of Celtics fans, a lot of Duke fans. It's always a good time coming back."

Throughout his career, Tatum has always flipped the switch in Charlotte. He's averaged 29.9 points with eight rebounds and 3.7 assists across 15 career games — not including Friday nights — against the Hornets on the road.

CHARLOTTE, NC – NOVEMBER 6: Jayson Tatum #0 of the Boston Celtics shoots the ball during the game against the Charlotte Hornets during the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on November 6, 2026 at Spectrum Center in Charlotte, North Carolina. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Kent Smith/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images

For as many 'MVP' chants as Tatum has drawn and will continue to draw this season, this performance certainly lived up to the billing. He did everything. He entered the night shooting 41.8 percent from the field and 22.9 percent from three before going 56.3 percent and 62.5 percent, respectively, in Charlotte.

"It was a pretty damn good night," Payton Pritchard told reporters, per CLNS Media. "34 is pretty good."

Tatum unleashed his dominance, both as a scorer and as a playmaker. He was the undisputed leader, carrying out a belt-to-backside thrashing that took Hornets head coach Charles Lee's group out of contention well before the game had reached its end.

He also got to the line plenty, going a perfect 11-for-11 from the charity stripe.

Pritchard continued: "He plays the right way, and he makes great decisions and [he's] one heck of a ball player for sure."

In each of his first eight appearances this season, Tatum has recorded six-plus assists.

It's been only eight months since Tatum returned from his ruptured Achilles tendon last season, which is much more recent than it might sound. He's still working toward completing his first full season since returning, and as much as he's continued to pass the eye test, Tatum still doesn't consider himself 100 percent just yet.

"Hell no," Tatum told CelticsBlog's Noa Dalzell. "I wish. I'm getting there, but no. How I felt before I got hurt was really, really good. I don't feel too far, and again, I still only played less than 40 games since I've been back, so still in the quote-unquote rehab phase of returning to play."

Still, he isn't discouraged by the process.

"We're gonna get there, though," Tatum added.

On Wednesday, the Celtics survived letting go of a 22-point lead against the Milwaukee Bucks as Tatum rested on the sidelines. In Charlotte, they witnessed Tatum make the most of his additional rest and take another step toward becoming the leader Boston will need this season.

#2826. Rams Add Dual-Threat RB, Two-Time Pro Bowler Amid Myles Garrett News

The Los Angeles Rams will officially have Myles Garrett on the field against the Washington Commanders in Week 9.

This will be Garrett's first game since Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. LA announced the news that they officially activated Garrett off injured reserve, along with several other roster transactions, on the eve of game day.

They also activated Ronnie Rivers from IR, sent Jaylen Watson to IR, and elevated two players.

"LA Rams Roster Moves," the team announced in a post on X on November 7, listing off their various actions:

Activated from Reserve OLB Myles Garrett, RB Ronnie Rivers

Activated, from Practice Squad (Standard Elevation) LS Jake McQuaide, CB Damarion Williams

The news on Garrett comes amid an insider report on the Rams' plan for the two-time and reigning Defensive Player of the Year, who has yet to record a stat this season following his blockbuster offseason trade from the Cleveland Browns.

"Rams star edge Myles Garrett is expected to return to action Sunday against the Commanders—and he could play a significant role," The Sweep's Tom Pelissero wrote on November 7, adding that fans should "expect Garrett to play on most passing downs and potentially work in on early downs, depending how he's feeling in his first game since undergoing knee surgery after Week 1."

Rivers suffered an injury in Week 2 against the New York Giants.

He returns just as the Rams have lost his replacement, Dean Connors, to IR due to a hand injury. Connors is an undrafted rookie free agent who impressed during the preseason.

A dual-threat back, Rivers is strictly on the Rams' 53-man roster as a special teams contributor as a distant RB3 behind Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. However, Rams head coach Sean McVay has spoken candidly about his trust in Rivers.

"I trust that he knows what he's doing, I trust his instincts, I trust his ability to be able to be effective in pass protection, get the ball where it's supposed to go in our different run schemes, and be a functional extension of the pass game," McVay told reporters in August. "We got two great running backs in Kyren and Blake that are going to be building on what they've done. But if for whatever reason they need to be supplemented, Ronnie Rivers is the guy that I trust."

McVay also tipped reporters to the Rams' plans for Watson.

The two-time Super Bowl champion injured his shoulder and it required surgery to address, ending his season.

Both McQuaide and Williams' additions for game day are due to injuries on the Rams' 53-man roster, somewhat undercutting the excitement around Garrett and Rivers' returns from the injured list.

Typical long snapper Joe Cardona is out with an ankle injury this week.

That is something McVay also suggested was possible if not likely earlier in the week. McVay noted that the two-time Pro Bowler, McQuaide, would get the nod.

The Rams signed Williams to their practice squad in October. He figures to slot in behind Emmanuel Forbes, Josh Wallace, and Cam Lampkin in some capacity. It is unclear what capacity, though, since Trent McDuffie is also questionable after not practicing this week.

In that sense, Williams' elevation is an ominous sign for the Rams amid Garrett's return.

Here's that and more before the Knights host the Knickerbockers tonight.

On Karl-Anthony Towns' strong start and the areas where he still needs to improve:

"I say those two things because he's been doing so many things well for us. He's rebounding, he's running, he' s shooting the ball well from 3, he is passing when he doesn't go for the home run ball, he's communicating. The energy he's bringing is great."

On Towns' professionalism amid his contract situation:

"Yeah, I didn't have any doubt on it, you know? And obviously the contract stuff, that's something that Leon [Rose] and at the end of the day, Jim [Dolan], will handle. On Towns' pick-and-roll defense, turnovers and overall performance:

"Man, I tell you what, KAT's been great. He has been great in practice. Really everything. It would be easier for him to say the areas that he needs to be better in. And the first one is just putting his chest in front of the ball in pick-and-roll situations and activity in that regard. And then not looking for the home run pass all the time when he has the ball as our hub. And I say those two things because he's been doing so many things well for us.

"He's rebounding. He's running. He's shooting the ball well from three. He is passing when he doesn't go for a home run all the time. He's communicating. So there's the energy that he's bringing that's great . . . So I'm really pleased with the way that KAT is playing overall."

On unexpectedly giving Dalton Knecht playing time against Chicago:

"It's just a gut feel. Like, [Knecht's] on my, quote-unquote, minutes sheet. He's down for zero minutes, you know?"

On Dalton Knecht's impressive debut and encouraging him to play aggressively:

"He played great. I think the way he was rebounding and getting out in transition, and just telling him to be aggressive no matter what the situation is. On the Knicks' title defense and his motivation to win another one:

"Being the No. 1 pick, [reaching] the Finals and getting your title, and having to go out there and try to figure out how to do it again, that's enough motivation for me."

On his rebounding numbers and compensating for Mitchell Robinson's departure:

"I just always want to impact winning, and I always try to get every rebound possible for our team so we don't give up any second-chance points or we give ourselves more chances at second-chance points on offense.

"Obviously, with [Mitchell Robinson] gone, I had to pick up the effort, especially the rebounding effort. When you have one of the greatest offensive rebounders the NBA has ever seen in Mitchell Robinson, it's a team effort. I just want to do my part to help with rebounding."

On putting the Knicks ahead of his contract situation and personal interests:

"Me and Jalen [Brunson] are here to lead the team. I want to do my part as best as I possibly can. I can't allow outside distractions and ego to get in the way.

#2819. Winners & Sinners: Week 3

Welcome to Winners & Sinners, where we reflect on the week that was for the Milwaukee Bucks. Week 3 saw the Bucks go 0-3, with the team losing to the Minnesota Timberwolves, Boston Celtics, and Toronto Raptors, despite some valiant efforts that put them in positions to win. But who's deserving of the hardware?

Prior to the Raptors game, this was a legitimate conversation between Myles Turner and Tyler Herro. Then Turner pulled one of his all-too-common vanishing acts. Meanwhile, Herro put in his best playmaking performance as a Buck to make it a no contest. And although he's struggled in first quarters—zero first-quarter points this week—it hasn't really mattered. He heats up. Quickly. But as Nate O. said in our staff thread, "he's definitely more than just a microwave—he's an air fryer."

And so the nickname was born: Tyler Herro, the Air Fryer. Please make this a thing.

The Contenders: Myles Turner, Ryan Rollins.

The Decision: I was so ready to anoint Turner as the defensive champion following his showings against the Timberwolves and Celtics, where he was a force blocking shots, accumulating seven across the two games, and also doing yeoman's work on the boards (at least for him). Then he made it look like the Bucks would have to give up picks in any swap for Jakob Poeltl. Rollins had his moments too, especially when hounding Derrick White. But this belt ain't no participation award; folks need to take it. And so it's still collecting dust in the locker room.

This week's champion is Sausagemahoney, who raised a very thought-provoking question about the Bucks' decision to take Brayden Burries over Yaxel Lendeborg, who's since given the zombie Golden State Warriors new life—and who legend Chris Mullin thinks is "going to be a perennial All-Star and just an All-NBA type":

Truthfully, I'm just jealous I didn't pose the question for this week's Bucks Reacts Survey.

If, prior to the season, someone told you that Nate Ament would play fourth-quarter minutes for the Bucks—not the Herd—in the third week of the season, you'd have assumed it would come in garbage time. If they told you he would be a key contributor in a 22-point comeback, splashing an above-the-break three-pointer to cut the lead to two, you'd have called them crazy. Yeah, the Bucks didn't go on to win this one. And, yes, the Bucks are in the trenches. But moments like this give you a reason to believe.

No hesitation, no rim. No ceiling. Not for this rookie.

Whoever coined "Kuzmania" absolutely nailed it—even if it was originally intended as a positive. Like "mania's" psychiatric denotation, Kyle Kuzma's game is just all over the place far too often for a tenth-year veteran. This week's case in point came at the 2:59 mark of the fourth quarter against the Boston Celtics when, after coming back from a 22-point deficit and down only two, Kuzma decides to take a corner three with 19 seconds left on the shot-clock. 19! It wasn't even as if he was hot—he'd hit only two field goals all game. Of course, after it clanks off rim, the Celtics go on to collect multiple offensive rebounds on the next possession, before Derrick White makes an and-one layup to extend the lead to five. Game over. But the most infuriating thing isn't even that it cost the Bucks the win, it's that Kuzma is supposed to be a veteran presence teaching the Bucks' youth. Some lesson.

If Taylor Jenkins moving Brayden Burries into the starting lineup is a signpost of his willingness to tinker, then he has to do so elsewhere too. There is absolutely no reason to continue to start Kuzma and play him heavy minutes. None!

That's all for Week 3. Share your winners and sinners in the comments!

#2816. Cowboys two keys to beating Colts and keeping playoffs hopes alive

The Dallas Cowboys have very possibly not yet defined what "rock bottom" could look like on this 2026 season, but any version of sinking lower than they are right now would involve a second straight loss to a losing team this upcoming Sunday afternoon. The Cowboys are at the Colts, who have not won in over a month.

Many things about this matchup make it feel like it's an opportunity sitting on a tee for Brian Schottenheimer's team to get back in the win column, and just maybe make the run-in to Thanksgiving interesting.

It's time for our weekly look at how the Cowboys can keep alternating wins and losses by bouncing back in week nine, or how they could send this season farther down the drain with another bad loss.

Old friend Daniel Jones at QB for the Colts is the next opponent for the Cowboys to put pressure on, both with their defense (more on that later) and ideally the offense too, by possessing the ball and scoring touchdowns. Jones is 1-8 in his career against the Cowboys, from his past time with the Giants, with four touchdowns and six interceptions in these nine games.

At all three levels of the Colts defense right now, they have problems. Up front, they just traded away DeForest Buckner. At linebacker, Akeem Davis-Gaither will be out on Sunday, with the team already starting rookie C.J. Allen at one of the linebacker positions. In the secondary, former Cowboy Charvarius Ward and Sauce Gardner have not played up to potential and are prone to being beat over the top, and committing costly penalties. Nickel defender Justin Walley is also ruled out against the Cowboys.

The Colts also have the worst turnover differential in the league this season, and have been minus three in two of their last three games, both divisional losses. They do not have a game with a positive margin, and their only neutral game was still a 34-22 loss to Mike McCarthy's Steelers.

With CeeDee Lamb telling the media this week he views the Cowboys offense as beating themselves more than anything, there should be no excuse to not execute the basics against the Colts. Not every drive has to end in points, but not having the focus to stay on the field in short-yardage situations, not getting backed up by unforced penalties, and not finding ways to get the ball to Lamb and George Pickens in space to lean on the Colts all afternoon with this highly-paid offense would be an abject failure.

The Colts defense has not taken the ball away once throughout their active four-game losing streak. If the Cowboys don't turn the ball over and give the Colts extra life and short fields to keep the game close, the talent differential in this matchup should reveal itself and allow the Cowboys to get out of Indy with a win.

Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor might be the obvious choice as the potential game-wrecker against the Cowboys defense in this matchup, especially considering the Colts main objective may actually be getting Taylor's trade value up with a big game against a Dallas defense torched by Tyler Allgeier last week.

Allgeier was certainly a big factor in how the Cardinals made their comeback in Arlington last Sunday, but when the game clearly came down to Gardner Minshew needing to make a throw, he did so as well for the real backbreaking plays against Christian Parker's defense.

The Cowboys also sacked Jacoby Brissett four times last week, but only got to Minshew once with Quinnen Williams doing so in overtime. Daniel Jones was sacked three times last Sunday against the Jags. He was sacked four times against a Vikings defense that blitzed him at a relentless rate that literally broke records for how often a defense could blitz. The week before that, he was sacked six times against the Titans. The Steelers defense only got to Jones once, but still swung the game in their favor by forcing Jones to drop back 44 times compared to 24 total rushing attempts for the Colts in week five.

In Jones' last four starts against the Cowboys, all losses, he's been sacked 16 times. Narrow this down to the last two games, and the Cowboys have won by a combined score of 60-15 with eight sacks, and also three interceptions.

Whether it's with the blitz or trusting Williams, Rashan Gary, and Donovan Ezeiruaku up front, Parker's defense needs to make pressure the priority against this Colts offense. The coverage is not good enough to hold up for long enough periods of time to be trusted more than the Cowboys should trust their ability to get to Jones before he can even throw the ball, and the same goes for run defense. Sacks to get the Colts behind the chains is what this defense should be after more than anything.

If the Cowboys continue to struggle finishing around the quarterback and allow Jones to extend plays, it will equally keep Jonathan Taylor as a threat in this game, and could make for a longer than anticipated afternoon trying to beat a team that's already waved a white flag.

#2814. Ankeny football coach recovering after scary sideline collapse

A scary moment occurred during the Iowa high school football state quarterfinal between Ankeny and Iowa City Liberty on Nov. 6.

Late in the fourth quarter, Ankeny defensive ends coach Greg Schoon collapsed on the Hawks' sideline. Several people in attendance, including police, athletic trainers from both teams and even fans who work in the medical field, came down to the field to assist with CPR and the use of a defibrillator until an ambulance arrived to take Schoon to a hospital.

After a delay, the game continued and the Hawks advanced to the state semifinals with a 51-29 win over Liberty.

Ankeny head coach Jeff Bauer told the Des Moines Register on Nov. 7 that he visited Schoon in the hospital following the game. Bauer said Schoon was "talking like normal coach Schoon" as the hospital ran tests. It was unclear what caused Schoon to collapse and he will remain in the hospital at least until Monday, Bauer said.

Bauer said the quick response from all who assisted was "amazing."

"We all said later, 'God, it's a blessing it happened there,'" Bauer said. "There's so many people there to help save you and they all went to action in no time."

Bauer said Ankeny players planned to visit Schoon in the hospital over the weekend. Ankeny will face Johnston on Nov. 13 at the UNI-Dome for a spot in the state finals as the program hopes for a speedy recovery for their beloved coach.

Eli McKown covers high school sports and wrestling for the Des Moines Register. Contact him at Emckown@gannett.com. Follow him on Twitter at @EMcKown23.

#2808. Falcons vs. Bengals series history: Win-loss record, matchup results

The Falcons head back into play against the AFC this week, and they do so across the pond in the second ever NFL game to be played in the Spanish capital of Madrid, at the esteemed Estadio de Santiago Bernebéu. Their opponent in that game will be the Cincinnati Bengals, who have won two games out of every three against the Birds, owning a very aesthetically pleasing 10-5 all time record against Atlanta.

The majority of that damage came before the turn of the millennia, with the Bengals winning seven out of 10 matchups against the overmatched Falcons through the 1996 season, with games between these teams happening on averaged every three years in that time period.

The Birds pulled back a little bit with three consecutive victories — in 2002, 2006 and 2010 — to pull the series close to even. That was quickly followed with three straight Bengals victories which brings us to where we are today, with two of those coming in the Matt Ryan era, which was also the most successful one in Falcons history. The Bengals caught Atlanta in a down year of that era twice in a row, in 2014 and 2018.

The Falcons had some confidence about them in year 2 of the Arthur Smith regime, having just pulled back to .500 at 3-3, with a victory against the 49ers after some questionable reffing cost them against Tampa the week before. The Bengals sported the same record, but they proved from the start that they were on another level.

It took exactly two minutes for second year man Joe Burrow to hit Tyler Boyd on a 60-yard touchdown to open the scoring. Then after a Falcon punt, the Bengals punched the ball in again following a longer drive. Then an Atlanta three and out was followed with a Burrow to rookie Ja'Marr Chase touchdown on the first play of the second quarter, before the two connected in the end zone again on the back end of the same quarter.

By halftime the game was effectively over as the Falcon offense spent the second half completely one dimensional and getting terrorized by the Bengal defense, with Burrow putting the finishing touches on with a rushing score to complete his magnificent day.

Up 35-17, one of the most impressive feats by the Bengal offense was getting the ball back via punt at their own 3-yard-line (why the Falcons punted it near midfield down three scores in the fourth quarter I don't know) with 8:44 left in the game and choking away that entire clock (and all three Atlanta timeouts) with a 17-play drive which went 95 yards and ended in a kneel down.

Hey, a win! The Brooklyn Nets entered Wednesday night's game against the Charlotte Hornets searching for their first home win of the season. Thankfully for them, it finally came thanks to a big fourth quarter run as Brooklyn came away with a 114-104 victory.

Now, Brooklyn takes that momentum on the road, beginning a four-game trip against an Atlanta team coming off an offensive explosion. The Atlanta Hawks are hoping to go far in the postseason this year and position themselves for a promising future. They helped the cause with a 139-132 victory over the Washington Wizards on Friday night.

Matchup: Brooklyn Nets (2-6) vs. Atlanta Hawks (6-4)

Watch: YES Network, DAZN, NBA League Pass

Questionable – Drake Powell (G-League assignment)

OUT – Mouhamed Gueye (left foot fracture)

OUT – Keshon Gilbert (left knee inflammation)

OUT – Asa Newell (left great toe hyperextension)

This night one of a back-to-back for Brooklyn. We'll see if anything changes before tip-off.

The Nets are on the first night of a back-to-back and first game of a four game road trip. They'll head to Dallas for a Sunday evening matchup with the Mavericks.

The Hawks are on the second night of a home back-to-back. They wrap up their brief three game homestand on Monday night against the Los Angeles Lakers. They hope to do something big this spring, but they have their doubters. From Ricky O'Donnell at the mothership:

"This team doesn't have enough force going to the basket, and the defense isn't anything special despite generating a lot of takeaways and forcing misses from three. The Hawks look mid as always."

It takes time to get used to someone in a new role. We've spent so much time with Nickeil Alexander-Walker being a solid bench role player that it's still somewhat surprising to see him operate as a high(er) usage wing as a starter. Alexander-Walker won the Most Improved Player award last year and he's carried that success over to this year. He's averaging a career best 22.3 points per game, and most impressively is getting to the line over four times a game. When Johnson returns, we'll see how the Hawks look to climb the standings.

Nolan Traore keeps stacking good days together. The second year guard had another good game as a starter on Wednesday night and he's making a great case to remain the starter once Egor returns. Traore can get to the rim and is second on the team in drives per game.

We'll get to watch a rookie who finally made his way into the starting lineup.

CJ McCollum requested that he come off the bench and the kid gets to start. With the Hawks looking to establish their future, a selfless decision like that from McCollum will go a long way in establishing Flemings as a key player going forward. For Atlanta, finding out what they have in Flemings will go a long way in determining their future. He's played over 23 minutes in four out of the last five games and with this being night two of the b2b, we'll see how long Quin Snyder plays him for.

Mikel Brown Jr is not on the injury report, so he'll play tonight and will more than likely sit tomorrow night in Dallas. The Nets are continuing to build Brown Jr and trust that his growth will lead to an exciting future. The drives are there, but if the three pointers start to become consistent, the sky is the limit for him and the Nets. It's all about making the most of the opportunities that are available to you.

Last weekend, the Atlanta Dream fell short in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals against the Golden State Valkyries. The last do-or-die game to decide the W Finals was a pretty celebratory occasion around these parts.

#2805. Who are the Steelers taking in expert mock drafts?

Is it too early to talk about the NFL Draft? There are always those that say "never," but for many, draft season doesn't start until the Steelers have played their last snap of the season in the early months of the new year.

However, Pittsburgh's bye week always presents a good time to take a step back from the storylines of the current season and evaluate the bigger picture. Just how good are the Steelers? What are their biggest roster needs? And who are some early targets in the upcoming 2027 draft?

With no game this weekend to distract from, here are six recent national NFL mock drafts and the Steelers' projected first-round selection in each. You can click on each pick's heading to read the full draft and see who was available when Pittsburgh was "on the clock."

Fox Sports' Rob Rang: Given the investment made in Drew Allar last spring, I don't believe the Steelers are planning to draft a quarterback in the first round of the 2027 draft. However, should an abbreviated 2026 season push Dante Moore — the most talented passer in this class — far enough down the board, it would make sense for Pittsburgh to adjust its plan.

A to Z Sports' Kyle Crabbs and Rob Gregson: While Jamel Dean, Asante Samuel Jr. and Daylen Everette have done a nice job this season, Ellis Robinson IV would transform that secondary. He's one of the most complete corners in this class, and he plays with a physicality and tenacity that scream Pittsburgh.

CBS Sports' Ryan Wilson: The Steelers need a QB. This is not up for debate. But do they roll with '26 third-rounder Drew Allar? Would, say, 6-foot-4 Austin Simmons make more sense here? Or does Mike McCarthy roll the dice on Chambliss, who is not 6-foot but has played a lot of high-level SEC football and is a proven winner?

USA Today's Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Grappling with the likes of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins is never fun for opponents. That's the Steelers' reality for the foreseeable future, however, and sending off Joey Porter Jr. only complicates that task. At 6-4 and 205 pounds, Jones combines the size to pester both well-built receivers and the speed to stick close by each one.

Sports Illustrated's Justin Melo: The Pittsburgh Steelers will probably transition to Will Howard or Drew Allar at quarterback next season. They should explore their potential post-Aaron Rodgers before spending another pick at quarterback. They could help their young starter by adding a workhorse running back like Florida's Jadan Baugh.

NFL Stock Exchange's Connor Rogers: "I think (the Steelers) offensive line has a lot of young talent, and it feels like they're probably pretty excited about Drew Allar after Aaron Rodgers — I'm not really thinking quarterback here yet. … I literally looked up DK (Metcalf's) contract wondering about (drafting Texas' Cam Coleman), but it's not pretty, so it's not happening here. … But when you watch Tae Johnson's 2025 tape, it's game-changing safety-level stuff. If he's healthy and comes back this year and returns to the form he had last year, this is well worth this selection.

The Steelers are currently on track to pick in the late-20s of the first round. Currently, the team has nine picks in 2027: one each in Rounds 1 and 2, two in Round 3, none in Round 4, one in Round 5 and two each in Rounds 6 and 7. The Steelers are not projected to earn any compensatory picks in 2027 according to Over the Cap.

Which of the above players caught your eye the most? Which position do you think the Steelers will target in the first round? Want to make any way-too-early predictions yourself? Join the BTSC community and let us know in the comments.

#2804. Gasperini’s Roma break scoring record: 31 goals in 11 games

Roma dominated Sassuolo and went up by three goals after just 58 minutes thanks to Hermoso (27′), Walukiewicz's own goal (30′), and Mora (58′).

The Giallorossi responded to the defeat in Manchester by displaying the character and spectacular play they've shown since the start of the season.

The Romans managed, with patience, to break down the wall that Aquilani attempted to build in front of Turato with a five-man defense when they didn't have possession.

After just 11 league games, the Giallorossi have already scored 31 goals: a record for Gian Piero Gasperini, as well as for the club.

The last Serie A team to have scored at least 30 times at this point in the season was Atalanta, coached by Gasperini from Grugliasco, in 2019-20. The Romans continue to surprise, a new milestone for Gasperini as well, who has found a way to maximize his players' performance in front of goal.
