#2801. Paderborn vs. Eintracht Frankfurt preview: Die Adler searching for third successive win

Competing in the top flight for the first time since 2019-20, Paderborn are sitting in 14th spot after winning two, drawing three and losing three of their eight league games. The second of those victories came in their most recent home outing, a 1-0 success over Hamburger SV on October 24.

However, they have failed to score since Rayan Philippe netted an 88th-minute winner against Hamburg. They fell to a 1-0 defeat to Stuttgart in the DFB-Pokal, before they played out a goalless draw in last Saturday’s away clash against Borussia Mönchengladbach.

While the goals have dried up, Paderborn can at least be pleased with the fact they have avoided defeat in each of their last three league games (W1, D2). However, the league’s second-lowest scorers know they will need to improve in the final third if they are to put distance between themselves and the drop zone, with Ralf Kettemann’s side currently sitting two points clear of the bottom three.

They can take some confidence from the fact they have won all three of their previous home meetings with Frankfurt, even if the most recent of those encounters took place nearly seven years ago in December 2019.

Mario Götze is unlikely to feature due to an ear infection, denying him the chance to face off against his brother Felix Götze. Hütter is also without Jessic Ngankam, while Robin Koch is a doubt due to a knee problem.

Frankfurt head into the weekend in eighth spot after winning three, drawing two and losing three of their eight Bundesliga matches. Die Adler took maximum points from last Sunday’s home clash against Hamburger SV, just a matter of days after beating the same opponent by the same 3-1 scoreline in the DFB-Pokal.

The league encounter was level at one goal apiece at half time before Raphael Onyedika and Younes Ebnoutalib found the net to fire Adi Hütter’s side to all three points. After enjoying a successful outing at Deutsche Bank Park, Frankfurt will now head on their travels with the minimum objective of avoiding a third consecutive away defeat in the Bundesliga.

Their ultimate goal will be to record their second away win of the season, although that would require them to beat Paderborn at the Home Deluxe Arena for the very first time. While a head-to-head away win has evaded them up until this point, they were victorious in the most recent meeting between the two sides in June 2020, when they held off a Paderborn fightback to clinch a 3-2 win.

The visitors are expected to be without Marcel Hoffmeier, Nyamekye Awortwie-Grant and Timur Gayret. In positive news, Sven Michel is available for selection after recovering from the injury that has kept him out of the last two matches.

#2800. Detroit Lions place LB Jack Campbell on injured reserve

In its Saturday afternoon roster moves, the Detroit Lions officially placed star linebacker Jack Campbell on injured reserve.

Campbell has been hospitalized after suffering a scary neck injury during last week's win over the Minnesota Vikings.

Campbell's injury appeared to happen on the first play of the fourth quarter as Campbell tackled Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson.

After the play, Campbell lay face down and motionless on the Ford Field turf. Eventually, Campbell was placed on a backboard, carefully lifted, and then carted off the field. The Lions initially reported that Campbell had been transported to a local hospital where he was set to be evaluated for a neck injury.

The Lions announced on Sunday evening that Campbell was resting and would remain in a local hospital overnight for continued evaluation and monitoring.

Campbell released a statement on Wednesday, providing an encouraging update on his improving status.

The 2025 first-team All-Pro and Butkus Award winner wrote in his statement, "I have full movement in my lower body, and I'm continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body."

"Jack continues to improve, which is all great news," Dan Campbell said of his star linebacker. "How would he prepare? How would he play? Those are the standards for us going into this game. We owe it to him."

As part of its roster moves, the Lions signed defensive back Nick Whiteside to the active roster from their practice squad. The Lions also elevated EDGE Anthony Lucas and running back Jabari Small from the practice squad.

#2799. 2026-27 NHL season predictions: Expert picks for Stanley Cup playoffs, champion and major awards this season

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Following a brief offseason and an expedited preseason, the 2026-27 NHL season has arrived. Before the puck drops on opening night, we have some predictions to make.

If this season feel like it's staring earlier than usual, that's because it is. The NHL is adopting an 84-game regular season, which just means more hockey for the rest of us. That also means a long and arduous journey to the Stanley Cup is ever so slightly more difficult.

So, what will that journey look like? The Carolina Hurricanes are looking to defend their title as Cup champions, but they'll have to contend with a deep Eastern Conference and some real juggernauts in the Western Conference. With that in mind, we logged our expert predictions for the playoff field in each conference -- and there were a few surprises -- before making our Stanley Cup Final selections.

We also called our shot on the winners of each major individual award. Connor McDavid is looking for his fourth Hart Trophy, but he's got some competition from an up-and-coming superstar in his own division. Races for the Norris Trophy and Vezina Trophy should be pretty wide open, and unexpected candidates always emerge throughout the season.

It should be a fun season in the NHL, so follow along with all our coverage at CBS Sports. Let's get things kicked off with the season preview and predictions, which will of course be 100% accurate.

Baumgartner: I don't see many new faces entering the conversation when it comes to the Eastern Conference playoff race. A healthy Florida Panthers side will slot themselves right back towards the top of the Atlantic, and a revamped Washington Capitals side should be able to make some noise in the Metropolitan. Besides that, I have six 2026 playoff teams returning to the dance in 2027.

Nivison: As much as I hate to go with chalk in preseason predictions -- because it rarely happens that way -- there's no denying the top dogs in the West. The Avalanche and Stars are the class of the Central Division, and the Golden Knights should pound a pitiful Pacific Division into a pulp. Things get more interesting behind those clear Cup contenders, and I'm projecting another significant leap forward from the Mammoth. I also think Macklin Celebrini will be successful in dragging the Sharks to the playoffs in his third NHL season.

Nivison -- Columbus Blue Jackets: The Blue Jackets have been agonizingly close to the playoffs in each of the last two seasons, and I think they get over the hump in 2026-27. There are still questions in Columbus. Can Adam Fantilli be a franchise player at center? Is the forward group as a whole good enough to keep pace in a competitive Eastern Conference? Still, I am sure the Blue Jackets have a really strong blue line, led by Norris Trophy winner Zach Werenski, and goaltender Jet Greaves is on track to become a Vezina Trophy candidate. Internal improvements from the young core will then get Columbus above the cut line.

Baumgartner -- San Jose Sharks: The Sharks narrowly missed out on the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs, finishing just four points short of the second wild card. San Jose added a good group of veterans over the summer, but the most important offseason move was selecting Ivar Stenberg with the No. 2 pick in the Draft. Stenberg joins the youth movement in San Jose, which is spearheaded by new captain Macklin Celebrini, who broke the Sharks single-season points record with 115 last season. The Sharks are a better team than they were last year, and with Celebrini entering his third season as a legit Hart Trophy contender, this team won't be fun to play against.

Nivison: Yes, the Mammoth have a brutal path coming out of the Central Divison, but just close your eyes and imagine this scenario with me. Logan Cooley becomes a superstar center. Dylan Guenther hits 50 goals. Dmitry Simashev asserts himself as a budding top-four defenseman. Anders Lee and Vincent Trocheck provide necessary veteran depth. Now open your eyes. Utah is your Western Conference champion.

Unfortunately for the Mammoth, they will run into a refreshed Panthers team that now has double-barreled Tkachuks. Last season, we found out that all it takes to stop Florida is to hope all of its key players miss significant time with injury. The long offseason was probably a blessing in disguise as it allowed the Panthers to get healthy, and that's bad news for everyone else. The structure in front of the crease will limit some of the volatility we saw from Jacob Markstrom in New Jersey, and Florida wins its third Stanley Cup in four years.

Baumgartner: Before last season, the Carolina Hurricanes' kryptonite was the Eastern Conference Final. The Hurricanes were able to overcome their demons and win the East before ultimately taking home the franchise's first Stanley Cup since 2006. In the West, the Dallas Stars have been running into the same problem. After three straight seasons ending in the Western Conference Final, the Stars regressed last postseason, flaming out in the first-round to the Minnesota Wild. The Central Division will once again be a gauntlet, but I'm ready for Dallas to take the next step and reach the Stanley Cup Final.

While Dallas has continued to fall short in recent years, the Panthers have done the opposite. The Panthers made three consecutive Stanley Cup Final appearances, winning back-to-back Cups in 2023-24 and 2024-25. Last season, Florida's three-peat attempt came to a halt on day one of training after captain Aleksander Barkov went down with a non-contact injury, tearing both the ACL and MCL in his right knee. An offseason of healing for Barkov, and the rest of the banged up Panthers, has the team refreshed entering September for the first time in years. With nearly the entire 2025 Stanley Cup winning core still on the team and Brady Tkachuk added to the fold, Florida looks ready to win its third Stanley Cup in four seasons.

Nivison: Celebrini should have won the Hart Trophy last season, but for some incomprehensible reason, he wasn't even a finalist. This year, Celebrini replicates that performance and gets San Jose to the postseason to take home his first MVP award at age 20. Hughes posts a career year in his first full season with the Wild, and Spencer Carberry gets his flowers for winning the Metro Division after missing the playoffs last year.

Baumgartner: McDavid's ability to take over a game was evident nearly every time he touched the ice last season. His 24 points (11 goals,13 assists) in the final 14 games of the regular season -- without Leon Draisaitl in the lineup -- was one of the many reasons I put him No. 1 on my Hart Trophy ballot. With just two years left on his current contract, desperation may start to kick in to get the job in Edmonton, which would lead to another MVP-caliber season. Barkov is healthy and the frontrunner to win his fourth Selke, and Dahlin will have another strong season to take home his first career Norris Trophy.

#2798. A Bears win on Sunday could catapult Caleb Williams back into the MVP race

Before the 2026 season started, Caleb Williams was seen as a dark-horse MVP candidate. He was coming off an exciting first year with Ben Johnson, with a highlight reel a mile long. He was the Madden cover athlete, and as the offseason progressed, the buzz around Caleb and the Chicago Bears kept building.

After they dropped a 50-burger in Week 1, the NFL shifted the hype train into high gear, and the Bears were the lead story on every NFL show.

But then Week 2 and Brian Flores' Minnesota Vikings defense came to town, and coupled with a steady downpour, Chicago's offense never got on track. Then a fourth-quarter hamstring injury as the Bears were driving inside the Minnesota 1o yard line would sideline Williams for the next three games, seemingly ending his Most Valuable Player chances.

The Bears went 2-1 in his absence, but since his return, Williams and the Bears haven't trailed in any of their three games, and he's completing 73.8% of his passes for 860 yards, 4 touchdowns, no turnovers, and a passer rating of 111.3.

The last two weeks, he diced up the defenses of the last two Super Bowl teams, and his MVP odds have shot back up according to our partners at FanDuel Sportsbook.

Right now, he's at +800 to win MVP, trailing only the Buffalo Bills' Josh Allen (+175), the Cincinnati Bengals' Joe Burrow (+450), the San Fransocso 49ers' Brock Purdy (+550), and the Jacksonville Jaguars' Trevor Lawrence (+600).

Earlier this week, we outlined how difficult it has been historically for a player to win the Most Valuable Player award after missing time during the season, but there is a precedent for him to do it, and another big game on Sunday Night Football could get him back in the conversation.

#2793. Highlights: Spurs handle Kings behind blazing three-point shooting

Coming off a thrilling win against the Dallas Mavericks, the Spurs traveled to Sacramento to take on the Kings in their first NBA Cup game of the season. From the opening tip, the Spurs' offense showed no rust from Wednesday. They outscored the Kings 38-29 in the first quarter and took a 19-point lead into halftime. Despite a low-scoring third quarter, the lead remained the same as the Kings' defense had no answer for the Spurs' hot shooting from three-point range. They shot 50% (15-30) after shooting an abysmal 15% (5-36) against Dallas. The Spurs ultimately won 124-109, and extended their winning streak to seven.

Victor Wembanyama followed up his career-best performance of 52 points, 24 rebounds, and 8 blocks with 30 points (10-for-18 FG, 4-for-6 3PT, 6-for-9 FT), 14 rebounds, 2 blocks, and 2 assists. Despite Wemby's Wilt Chamberlain-esque performance this past Wednesday, his three-point shooting was forgettable (1-8 3PT). Wemby quieted the critics who have wanted him to stop shooting threes by shooting a scorching 66% on four-for-six against the Kings.

Stephon Castle, Dylan Harper, and Devin Vassell each dropped 19 points to balance out the Spurs' offensive attack. It was a great sign to see Devin light the nets on fire after going almost scoreless against Dallas. His ability to spread the floor and get to his spots helps the three guards penetrate and kick out to him for an easy three-point laser. In some cases, his range might surprise you.

This is when the team's offense is at its best. Swinging the rock around and punishing the defense with open threes and great looks inside.

#2792. Takeaways from FSU's win over Boston College

Florida State has finally done it. They broke their 12-game road losing streak on Saturday against the Boston College Eagles with a 31-24 win. Their last victory away from Doak Campbell Stadium came in their season finale in 2023 against the Florida Gators.

The Seminoles also ended a three-game losing streak for the 2026 season, with their last win coming against the Virginia Cavaliers a month ago. At 4-5 on the season, FSU now needs two wins in their final three games to become bowl eligible.

This was a good win for interim head coach Rick Stockstill to build off of, although it wasn't always pretty. Here are five takeaways from Florida State's win, which fired up their fans.

Thomas took full advantage of his increased workload as RB2 behind Quintrevion Wisner. He ran for 98 yards on 19 carries and scored two touchdowns as he led FSU's rushing attack that picked up 202 yards on the day. The explosiveness on the open field and the ability to run between the tackles is a dynamic that the Seminoles need to feature going forward.

Florida State needed Danzy to step his game up with Duce Robinson going down for the year with a torn ACL. He put up 86 yards on seven receptions, and several of them came in key moments to keep momentum going. Now, it's clear that he can handle being the top target in the passing game.

The true freshman was put into the starting lineup and immediately made an impact. Not only did he haul in four passes for 54 yards, which included key catches that moved the chains, Lopez also had a huge punt return for 40 yards at the end of the first quarter that set up FSU's first touchdown. He certainly needs more touches over the next three weeks.

Sims got his first chance to call plays as the interim defensive coordinator on Saturday. Boston College did run for 148 yards and convert eight of their 14 third-down attempts, but Sims and his play calling held them to seven points in the second half, and once he started to bring more pressure, it led to the Seminoles getting four sacks and two interceptions. This was a good building block for him.

This was an inspired performance from FSU after the chaos from firing Mike Norvell and other coaches last week. To have the resolve to go and end a road losing streak that's been going on since the beginning of 2024 with an interim coach was big. They don't play any juggernauts the rest of the way, which means this win might lead to a great ending to a roller coaster season.

#2790. What we learned from the Spurs’ win over the Kings

Before the season and even into the first few games, critics have questioned the San Antonio Spurs' four-guard starting lineup. However, through 9 games, that lineup has a +25.4 net rating in 95 minutes and has led the Spurs to a 7-2 start. The bench lineups, especially those without Victor Wembanyama, have caused the team issues. That was never more apparent than in San Antonio's 124-109 thrashing of the Sacramento Kings on Friday night.

Let's be honest about the Kings for a moment. They are a bad basketball team, perhaps not in talent, but in discipline and execution. They lose people on defense and take errant shots on offense. Yet, multiple times on Friday, they gained back ground with most of San Antonio's starters off the floor.

Most of San Antonio's mistakes come from defense, where too often players, especially on the wings, overhelp on a drive or watch the ball, letting the offensive player get an open three or cut to the rim and score over the top of Luke Kornet. San Antonio's defensive lapses were a big reason the Kings shot 49% from the field and hit 46% from three. That second unit's defensive issues don't flip the game against the worst in the league, but against a legitimate, deep team, it could lead to a loss.

The Spurs will take a 15-point win on the road in their first NBA Cup game. But it's hard to come out of that game feeling overly confident about the performance. San Antonio has won seven games in a row, but over half of those have come against teams under .500. A real test awaits them on Saturday in the red-hot Portland Trail Blazers. The Spurs' second unit will need to step up its defensive play if they want to compete with another Western Conference leader.

Devin Vassell is one of the most important players on the Spurs. Vassell is shooting 34.1% from three this season, well below his usual average, which has hurt San Antonio's offense. When he's hitting shots, like he did against Sacramento, the offense opens up a ton for the guards and Wembanyama to dominate the paint. Vassell had 19 points, hitting 5 of his 6 threes on Friday. His off-ball defense was solid, too. He did about all you can ask from a glue guy in the starting lineup. San Antonio will need more performances like these moving forward.

The Kings ran one of the weakest zones I've seen this season, and it led to a big run from the Spurs in the first half. That said, it made me realize that San Antonio is basically built to bust zone defenses. One, Wembanyama is kind of the ultimate cheat code to beat a zone. He can stretch it out on the perimeter or punish smaller players who get caught helping around the basket in the zone. Then, the Spurs have dynamic playmaking guards who are big and physical and can operate in the middle of the zone, a common weak spot in many zone defenses. Add in a couple of knockdown shooters like Vassell and Champagnie, and it becomes nearly impossible to run zone against San Antonio. The Kings tried, and failed to do so on Friday.

Stephon Castle had a rough defensive night, but made up for it with some of the best playmaking we've seen from him this season. He had 19 points, 7 assists, and 1 turnover in the win. One of those assists came on a beautiful inverted pick-and-roll with Wembanyama as the ball handler and Castle as the screener. Castle caught the ball on the short roll, did a 180-degree turn, and fired the ball to a wide-open Vassell for three. It was as close to the Beautiful Game Spurs as San Antonio got on Friday.

Harrison Barnes has earned his spot in the rotation lately, and one could argue he should be getting more minutes than some other bench forward on the roster. He had 13 points on 4-for-7 shooting on Friday against his former team. Offensively, he's a savvy connective player who can take advantage of a defense that is out of position after one of the Spurs' guards creates an advantage. He looks more like the Barnes we saw in his first season with San Antonio, rather than last year. He has essentially replaced Carter Bryant in the rotation, and it doesn't look like he will be giving up that spot any time soon with how he is playing.

I'm interested to see how this team will look once Tobias Harris comes back (hopefully this month?). They desperately need another shot creator and capable defender in that second unit. I know a lot of people want to see him replace Vassell in the starting lineup, but it seems like he could provide even more value as one of the first subs in the game, then playing for a prolonged stretch alongside Kornet and one or two of the guards. The Spurs' top free-agent acquisition should give them more of the versatility many thought the team would have going into the season.

#2788. Norris grabs pole in rainswept qualifying for Sao Paulo Grand Prix

McLaren's outgoing world champion Lando Norris grabbed pole position for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix with a brave and well-judged drive in Saturday's rainswept qualifying at Interlagos.

The 26-year-old Briton clocked a best lap in one minute and 27.470 seconds to outpace George Russell of Mercedes by 0.204 seconds as heavy rain curtailed Q3 at the end of a session that lasted almost two and a half hours.

New world champion Kimi Antonelli was third for Mercedes, but he will start Sunday's race from the front row as Russell faces a five-place grid penalty for taking new power-unit components.

It is the 20th pole position of Norris's career and his third in succession in Brazil.

"It's been a great qualifying, to be on pole again here, two years in a row! Different conditions to last year, but I am very happy.

"It was about getting two laps in and not making a mistake and that is exactly what we did so it has been a very good day."

Russell was disappointed not to take pole after being told by Mercedes to ease off on his final push lap.

"Congrats to Lando, but it was definitely my pole lap. We should have finished the lap."

Antonelli said: "It was very tricky out there and, to be fair, I didn't know what to expect as I have never driven here before in the wet. I made a mistake and I nearly went off!"

Charles Leclerc was fourth for Ferrari but also faces a penalty of 10 places for taking a new engine.

Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson was fifth ahead of Audi's Nico Hulkenberg, Isack Hadjar of Red Bull and Oliver Bearman's Haas.

Two-time champion Fernando Alonso was ninth for Aston Martin and Alex Albon 10th for Williams.

Seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton of Ferrari qualified 11th, but also faces a penalty for taking two new engines on Saturday and will start from the back of the grid while four-time champion Max Verstappen, who also has a 20-place penalty, was 16th for Red Bull.

The session began after a 90-minute delay in treacherous conditions with high plumes of spray rising from the cars.

Valtteri Bottas led out in his Cadillac with a 1:42.314 to set the bar with team-mate Sergio Perez soon improving on that before Haas's new boy Brazilian Rafael Camara hit the barriers, but continued.

Verstappen then went top ahead of Hamilton as conditions improved. Aware that there was more rain on the way, the teams warned their drivers that these were the best conditions.

Remarkably, they completed Q1 with Norris on top in 1:30.939, Camara through in 13th and both Alpines eliminated along with Lance Stroll of Aston Martin, both Cadillacs and local hero Gabriel Bortoleto who damaged his Audi's rear wing.

For Pierre Gasly it was his first Q1 elimination this year.

Verstappen, set to start from the back of the grid after taking a new power unit, decided not to go out again and instead saved his tyres.

In the end, a red flag halted Q2 when Camara smacked the wall at Juncao, leaving Russell on top ahead of Lawson while Hamilton, set for his 400th Grand Prix, went out in 11th with McLaren's Oscar Piastri, Camara, Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad and Carlos Sainz of Williams.

Antonelli survived in 10th while Alonso made Q3 for the first time this season.

Alonso led the queue, but he did not have the pace as Norris and then Russell went top as the rain arrived and Norris regained the initiative.

#2787. NFL Week 9 predictions: 4 game picks for the Seahawks vs. Cardinals rematch

The Seattle Seahawks return to Lumen Field on Sunday to face the Arizona Cardinals in a divisional matchup with plenty of betting opportunities. Seattle enters as an 8.5-point favorite, with the game total set at 39.5 points, according to FanDuel Sportsbook.

The Seahawks have had an inconsistent season, but Arizona's defensive struggles create some interesting opportunities on both sides of the ball. The Cardinals have allowed 29 touchdowns through eight games, the most in the NFL. That could open the door for Seattle's offense, particularly in the red zone.

Here are four bets/game picks worth considering ahead of Sunday's game.

Jadarian Price is an interesting option to find the end zone against Arizona. The rookie has shown the potential to turn an ordinary running lane into a big play, and Seattle's recent investment in its offensive line could help him find more opportunities to showcase that ability.

Against a defense that has struggled throughout the season, those opportunities could translate into a touchdown.

There is one important caveat, though: Price needs to take better care of the football. His fumbles have been a concern, and another mistake could limit his opportunities. If he can protect the ball, his explosiveness gives him a legitimate chance to make an impact on the scoreboard.

Trey McBride is one of the most reliable pass-catching tight ends in the NFL, and Seattle has historically struggled to contain him. The coverage behind Seattle's linebackers has been a recurring issue, particularly when opponents attack the intermediate areas of the field.

McBride is exactly the type of player who can take advantage of that weakness. He's a dependable target, consistently finds space in coverage and gives his quarterback a reliable option when the pocket gets uncomfortable. Arizona should have plenty of reasons to involve him throughout the game, especially if Seattle prioritizes preventing explosive plays elsewhere.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba should be one of Drew Lock's most important weapons on Sunday. The two have shown good chemistry, and that connection could become particularly valuable against an Arizona defense that has struggled to consistently defend the passing game.

Smith-Njigba can help Seattle address one of its biggest offensive concerns: finishing drives in the red zone. He was an important part of the solution in the first meeting between these teams, and the Seahawks should look to get him involved again when the field becomes shorter.

His value isn't limited to the red zone, either. Smith-Njigba has also been a dangerous deep threat throughout the season, capable of creating separation and turning downfield opportunities into explosive plays. That versatility makes him an especially valuable target for Lock, who will need reliable options to keep the offense moving.

With their established chemistry and JSN's ability to contribute at every level of the field, there's a good case for backing him to find the end zone.

This might be the most difficult bet to evaluate, largely because of the uncertainty surrounding Drew Lock. However, I don't see much of a middle ground in this matchup.

If Lock struggles, Seattle could have a difficult afternoon. Turnovers, particularly interceptions, could give Arizona short fields and keep the Cardinals in a game where they might otherwise struggle to keep pace offensively.

On the other hand, Lock could deliver another performance similar to his first meeting against Arizona. If he protects the football, establishes a rhythm with Smith-Njigba and takes advantage of Seattle's improved offensive line, the Seahawks have enough talent to win comfortably and cover the spread.

The Cardinals' defensive struggles make the second scenario entirely possible. Seattle has the weapons to create separation on the scoreboard, but everything depends on which version of Lock shows up.

I'm willing to take the risk because I believe Seattle has a significant advantage if its quarterback plays a clean game.

#2786. Luka Doncic's historic run jump-starts early MVP conversation

Ten games is too early for most valuable player conversation. Just don't tell fans at Crypto.com Arena.

"M-V-P! M-V-P!" the Lakers faithful chant at Luka Doncic every time the Lakers guard toes the free-throw line.

After dropping a season-high 53 points during the Lakers' 124-118 win over the Portland Trail Blazers on Friday, Doncic is averaging 40.1 points, 7.8 rebounds and 7.7 assists in a scoring binge for the ages. He's the fourth Laker to have four consecutive games of 40 or more points. He's the third to have seven games of 35 or more points.

And he's doing it efficiently: Doncic's sky-high shooting percentage dipped to 49.8% after an unusually cold 5-for-15 shooting night from three-point range Friday. He was still 12 for 18 from two-point range.

Here are three takeaways from Friday's win:

Lakers guard Luka Doncic shouts after sinking a three-pointer that gave the Lakers a five-point lead over Portland in the third quarter Friday at Crypto.com Arena. (Gina Ferazzi / Los Angeles Times)

Walker Kessler just shook his head as he grasped for the right words. There might not be many more left to describe what Doncic is doing.

"He's my MVP," the Lakers center said eventually.

Being in the most valuable player conversation isn't new for Doncic. The two-time scoring champion finished third in MVP voting in 2024 with Dallas. He averaged 33.9 points, 9.2 rebounds and 9.8 assists during the regular season, then led the Mavericks to the NBA Finals.

Each season the do-it-all guard is among the favorites to win the award. But Doncic's early-season campaign feels different. Not only is Doncic in great shape, Portland coach Micah Nori said before Friday's game, but Doncic also has the right pieces around him after the Lakers remade their roster to complement the star with floor-spacing shooters, strong perimeter defenders and a rolling center.

"It's a perfect offensive storm," Nori said. "He's the MVP right now. Hands down."

Lakers coach JJ Redick does not engage in MVP discussion until 50 games in, he said. When told Doncic topped NBA.com's first MVP ladder Friday, the Lakers coach brushed aside any chance to make a grand proclamation.

In the premature MVP rankings, Doncic was ahead of San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama. The 22-year-old is averaging 29.1 points, 12.6 rebounds, three assists and 4.2 blocks per game.

Doncic's 53-point outburst eclipsed Wembanyama's 52 points the star center scored Wednesday for the highest single-game scoring performance this season. But Wembanyama also grabbed 24 rebounds with eight blocks in a historic statline matched only by Wilt Chamberlain.

The French superstar finished second in MVP voting last year and was the first unanimous defensive player of the year in league history. His outsized defensive impact was a significant part of why he entered the season as the betting favorite to win his first MVP.

Read more: Swanson: Luka Doncic can lead Lakers to a title, but only if his teammates pull their weight

Doncic, who didn't get any votes from NBA general managers when asked in a preseason survey who they thought would win the MVP, said he's determined to step up on defense for his team. He is averaging 1.7 steals per game, which ranks second among Lakers players. His four drawn charges is tied for most in the league.

"He has a pride and he has a hunger," Lakers forward Sandro Mamukelashvili said of Doncic's defense. "He has a will to not be labeled as that guy who you can just attack."

Doncic is challenging Chamberlain's stats on the offensive end. His 361 points through his first nine games are the most for a player since Chamberlain's 472 points in 1962-63. No one has averaged 40 points over a season since the legendary center in 1963. The possibility has barely crossed Doncic's mind.

"As long as we win, I'm good," Doncic said.

The Lakers are 8-2 with the best record in the Western Conference. They have not started 8-2 since their last championship season.

Lakers forward Adou Thiero drives to the basket between Portland's Scoot Henderson (00) and Jrue Holiday (5) at Crypto.com Arena on Friday. (Gina Ferazzi / Los Angeles Times)

Adou Thiero had a loud four points, four rebounds and two assists in his long-awaited season debut Friday. The energetic forward missed the first nine games of the season because of swelling in his left knee. He didn't waste any time reintroducing himself to the team, keeping a loose ball alive on his first offensive possession that led to an offensive rebound and a put-back from Mamukelashvili.

"He literally did everything we asked him to do," Redick said.

The second-year forward has been hampered by his balky left knee since college, when he missed the end of his junior season after surgery. The procedure delayed the beginning of his rookie season and when he returned, a sprained MCL in his right knee knocked him out for six more weeks.

The injuries prevented Thiero from gaining any traction. This summer, when he had the longest stretch of sustained health during his short professional career, he could finally show teammates and coaches what he could do.

Thiero jumped out of the gym during practices. He smothered teammates while guarding the ball. He brought the same energy to the court Friday when it counted.

"We value Adou a lot," Kessler said. "He's a very physical player, really talented, athletic player."

Lakers forwards Ziaire Williams, left, and Sandro Mamukelashvili double team Portland guard Sidy Cissoko as he attempts a layup at Crypto.com Arena on Friday. (Gina Ferazzi / Los Angeles Times)

The Lakers missed their first 15 three-point shots. It felt like a minor miracle they trailed by only seven at halftime.

The most dynamic offense in the league had to rely on its defense. The Lakers forced 24 turnovers and held the Trail Blazers (6-2) to 15 points in the third quarter.

"It's nice to know when you're not making shots that you can also rely on your defense to help keep you in the game," said forward Jake LaRavia, who had seven points, eight rebounds and one steal.

The Lakers rank 21st in defensive rating, giving up 113.6 points per 100 possessions. They are one of the worst rebounding teams in the league, ranking 29th despite outrebounding the Trail Blazers by three. Their defense instead relies on blocks and steals.

The Lakers are tied for third in the NBA with 10.7 steals per game. Matisse Thybulle leads the team with 1.8 steals per game. Austin Reaves had a team-high four steals Friday.

#2785. Wales let themselves down despite win - Lake

Captain Dewi Lake says Wales let themselves down during the lacklustre 28-21 Nations Championship victory against Japan in Cardiff.

Josh Adams added two tries to scores from prop Archie Griffin and wing Louis Rees-Zammit as Wales claimed a bonus-point win.

This was their second victory from four games in the competition but Lake was left frustrated with aspects of the performance.

"There were massive parts of that game where we let ourselves down," he said.

"Getting into camp, we said we were going to do things that we probably didn't do against Japan.

"That's disappointing but this is a group that wants to grow and will challenge each other."

Nations Championship: Wales edge Japan but underwhelm - reaction

Wales labour to bonus-point win against Japan

In front of a crowd of 52,425 supporters, Wales had to hold on for only the fourth win in Steve Tandy's 13 Tests in charge, two of which have come against Japan.

Lake said a victory should not be underestimated with Wales having suffered recent losing streaks, which included a record 18 consecutive Test defeats in a row.

"A win is massive for this group, for the confidence and trust we'll get in each other," he said.

"We were happy with the win and it's something we've not done often enough, so I am proud of the boys."

Wales remain fifth in the northern hemisphere table but face much tougher challenges this month.

New Zealand, fresh from defeating Scotland, are the visitors to Cardiff next Saturday before Australia play at the Principality Stadium on 21 November.

"If you look at the two Test matches, we did things today that weren't good enough to compete in those games," said Lake.

"We'll have to get a lot right next week and fix some stuff."

Head coach Tandy said he was expecting more from his side this weekend.

"It's good to start the campaign with a bonus-point win but I can't run away from the performance when I talk about it," said Tandy.

"There are elements of the performance we definitely need to improve. I thought we'd be better than that in some elements.

"There was good stuff from us, in terms of the line breaks and how we opened Japan up, but we weren't ruthless enough.

"We'll definitely have to do that for the next couple of games but it helps to review after a win."

Japan head coach Eddie Jones said it was an opportunity missed to win a first game in Cardiff against Wales.

"That could have been a historic win for us but you've got to be good enough to take advantage of those mistakes," he said.

"We weren't quite good enough and it was certainly a missed opportunity."

Jones said he was proud of his young team but believes they needed to be more clinical.

"If you watch rugby now, once you get in the 22 and if you don't take points from that, that's the difference in the game," said Jones.

"We had three opportunities but we didn't take chances and Wales did. Their points-per-entry was higher than ours."

Jones questioned some aspects of the interpretation of New Zealand referee Paul Williams at the contact area.

"I hope I'm not going to get in trouble for this but there was one penalty for not supporting your weight at the breakdown and it was against us," said Jones.

"Anyone watching that game, can you think there was just one ruck where the supporting player was off his feet?

"That can be the difference between winning and losing.

"I'm not complaining, I'm just saying sometimes you don't get the rub of the green.

"That can happen. You've got to suck it up and get on with it. Actually maybe I am complaining!"

Japan travel to face Jones' former England side at Allianz Stadium at Twickenham next Saturday.

#2783. Oso Ighodaro is starting; is that a good thing?

The Phoenix Suns moved Oso Ighodaro into the starting lineup for Thursday's win against the Orlando Magic. Many called for a change to the lineup (or multiple changes, which is another article for another day). He is a somewhat polarizing player, with staunch fans and outspoken skeptics. I'll make a case for this being absolutely the right move for this team, right now.

Khaman Maluach is learning game by game. Working on his body (and hopefully hands) to get stronger. He has an awesome frame and, at 20 years old, is just beginning to learn the nuances of NBA success. He has a mostly high effort level and wants to be good. However, the NBA is littered with players thrust into action before developing properly – and then losing confidence, picking up bad habits. Time on the court in meaningful minutes is needed to progress toward the objective of becoming a solid NBA starting center. The current situation with Mark Williams out well into 2027 allows for consistent 15-20 minute nights. Handing the "starter" keys could put him on a path more closely aligned to former Suns top-10 pick Josh Jackson (sorry to those with draft PTSD here).

Back to Oso. The Phoenix starting lineup needs more connectivity and flow on offense? Check. Struggling horrifically on defense? Check. Per HoopsJunkie.io, Ighodaro's on/off defensive rating of -17.2 points per 100 possessions ranks EIGHTH in the NBA! This is in spite of being a below-average defensive rebounder (141st in the NBA in DREB%). Keep in mind, he suffered a right oblique strain in the opener and is likely just rounding back into form now. I've referenced DARKO several times as a great tool to project overall player value at a moment in time.

Through last season, his projected value was steadily growing. Once fully healthy, it is reasonable to expect that progression to continue. He looks bigger and stronger. His turnovers are down. While the results are not there yet at the free-throw line, he looks smoother (and commentators have noticed the same). With a DARKO of 1.0, compared to a -1.6 for Maluach, the model predicts more positive impact on winning in the present.

Oso and Ryan Dunn, to an even greater extent early this season, are developing players. They show what development can look like for players drafted 40th and 28th, respectively. With his raw talents (drafted 10th) and willingness to work, Maluach's ultimate success depends on development done the right way. This franchise needs Man Man to get there for the long run – and needs Oso right now to stabilize a starting lineup that was in disarray.

#2781. 49ers Mailbag: Should the team get more defensive line help? What’s up with the return/kicking game?

What? You mean you guys like these things?

We haven't done too many mailbags this year, but maybe I can change that. Because of the timing, I wasn't able to get to every question asked in my call for submissions, but keep an eye out for the next one. I post over in the Niners Nation Feed when I'm going to do a mailbag, and I'll be sure to not do it on a Thursday this time. By the way, if you haven't gone to The Feed yet, what's stopping you? Not only am I there, but Fooch posts there a lot, too. Come hang out with the Niners Nation alum!

Now, as for this week, this is going up Saturday afternoon, and the San Francisco 49ers are preparing for the Las Vegas Raiders. This seems like another tricky game for the team. Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins always seems to play well against the 49ers, like some long-standing grudge against Kyle Shanahan when the former was going to come in a few years before the latter traded for Jimmy Garoppolo. I think the 49ers can pull off the victory—based on the Raiders starting to remember they are the Raiders—but they can't make the same mistakes they did against the Atlanta Falcons.

If a Pontiac and a Buick both leave Chicago at the same time……….

They both will have engine failure two miles outside of city limits.

And keeping with the STs theme — why do they still have faith in Cowing returning punts? I'm terrified he's gonna drop it, even on a fair catch. If the former Ram who's on the practice squad isn't any better, why do we even have him on the team?

Probably because they don't want to pull from the very limited pool of wide receivers they already have and risk someone else getting beat up on the return game. I have to think that as the wide receivers come back, the 49ers move to…well…moving on from Cowing. At least at returner. They have Brandin Cooks on the roster, and while he's not as fast as he was a decade ago, he's still got some wheels and has been a returner in the past. De'Zhaun Stribling could also be a good option, but for reasons I just outlined, they may want him fresh for the offense and not on return duty because they aren't going to be able to rely on Mike Evans for every play.

I can't fathom a situation where Cowing is the punt returner in January based on what we've seen. This isn't even about his ball security issues; it's about his decision-making.

I'm of the mind that our D line is pretty awesome with Defo and Bosa on the field. My only reservation is injuries, especially Bosa. Do we really need to make a splash with an extra Edge? White, Williams and Height seems like a good rotation across from Bosa.

It could help, but I also think the 49ers need to hold onto some draft picks and salary cap space. Whoever they bring in, they have to make room for by releasing someone else, allocating what is the thinnest of margins in cap space, and sacrificing development of their younger talent. Not to mention draft picks. It's not the greatest answer, but when they bring in a Khalil Mack or some sort, that's going to take snaps away from a younger player who needs that experience and fewer picks to get more ammo in case that younger player doesn't work out.

I want to win now, just like all of you do, but not at the cost of development to stay competitive. I am not a fan of the Los Angeles' Rams way of just "buying" a Super Bowl for one year. Some players you know won't click; others need to be on the field and mess up, even in a championship season. The DeForest Buckner trade was great because while it removed snaps, it didn't do so much that it tossed the depth chart to the bench. Adding more could make things cramped. It also helped with the culture since Buckner has been there before and can be a good mentor

Speaking of which, that has already been paying dividends for young talent. Romello Height is getting up a bit earlier now, for one thing. The others have a lot to learn from Buckner as a player, and it's already rubbing off.

Has something changed in Piñeiro's mechanics, or with the snap and hold timing? Is he more accurate from one hash mark or another? How does he compare to the league average percentage of missed extra points? Why hasn't the team brought in another kicker for a tryout?

Why haven't they brought someone else in? Probably because Piñeiro just signed an extension with $10 million in guaranteed money. Kyle Shanahan did seem a bit miffed after the Atlanta game, but shortly after that, John Lynch affirmed the 49ers were sticking with Piñeiro. If you were wanting kicker tryouts—those aren't happening.

Have we hit David Akers or even Jake Moody levels of kicking? It's a rough patch, but I give him a couple more games. If he misses more XPs in the next two games, regardless of whether it's a victory or loss, the 49ers have to do something. It's just like if their punt returner had bad ball security and they did nothing…

Brandon Aiyuk owes the 49ers $13 million. If you'd signed that contract, what would you have spent the $13 million on?

I'd go to Vegas and make max bets on Casino War while getting bottle service. I'd set aside half for an executive suite at Levi's Stadium for one game. I'd also buy a sealed copy of Panzer Dragoon Saga for the Sega Saturn. If there's money leftover I'll also buy a gold cart of Nintendo World Championships.

#2777. 2. Bundesliga: Dresden off the bottom with convincing victory over Fürth

First half goals from Robert Wagner and Ben Bobzien had the hosts firmly in control at the half. Vincent Vermeij added a second-half strike to make it 3-0 before Hendry Blank saw red for the visitors capping off a miserable evening for Fürth. Dresden made a lively start at the Rudolf-Harbig-Stadion, although Greuther Fürth initially looked dangerous going forward. The visitors came close to opening the scoring through Omar Sillah, whose effort drifted narrowly wide after a defensive mix-up, before Sacha Bansé tested Lennart Grill with a powerful effort from distance. Dynamo also threatened at the other end, with Patrice Čović missing a promising opportunity from inside the penalty area.

However, it was the hosts who eventually broke the deadlock in the 31st minute. Niklas Hauptmann did well to turn away from two opponents before laying the ball into the path of Robert Wagner, whose first-time effort took a deflection off Hendry Blank and wrong-footed goalkeeper Florian Hellstern.

Dynamo doubled their advantage ten minutes later, with Ben Bobzien finding the net in similarly fortunate circumstances. After receiving the ball from Tobias Raschl, the forward cut inside before seeing his effort deflected by Blank and loop into the top corner, leaving Hellstern with little chance of making a save.

Fürth almost reduced the deficit before the interval, with Sillah narrowly missing a cross from Gian-Luca Itter before the latter saw two efforts blocked and deflected wide. Despite those opportunities, Thomas Stamm's side headed into the break with a deserved two-goal advantage.

The hosts continued to apply pressure after the restart and effectively put the contest beyond doubt in the 55th minute. Bobzien turned provider this time, setting up Vincent Vermeij, who had the simple task of rolling the ball into an unguarded net to make it 3-0.

Fürth's evening then went from bad to worse seven minutes later when Blank received his marching orders. Having already been booked in the opening minute, the defender brought down Bobzien as he threatened to break through on goal, receiving a second yellow card and leaving the visitors with ten men for the remainder of the contest.

Dresden looked increasingly comfortable against their numerical disadvantage, with Čović coming close to adding a fourth in the 73rd minute, only for his effort to be blocked by Krisztián Keresztes close to the goal line.

The hosts ultimately saw out a convincing 3-0 victory, recording another impressive home result following their recent wins over Magdeburg and in the cup against Schalke. The three points also provide a significant boost to Dresden's hopes of climbing away from the bottom of the 2. Bundesliga table, while Fürth will be disappointed with an evening in which defensive misfortune and Blank's dismissal contributed to a heavy defeat.

#2776. Maryland football survives late scare in 34-29 victory over Purdue

With Purdue down to a fourth-and-10 from their own 5-yard line and 44 seconds remaining, it appeared Maryland football's first Big Ten victory in 14 games was secured.

"They don't make it easy on me, man," interim head coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim joked of his defense after the game.

Purdue found a completion to extend its two-minute drill, and it kept moving downfield, arriving at Maryland's 11-yard line with five seconds left.

But an illegal substitution pushed the offense back, giving Maryland's pass rush more time to deliver. And as quarterback Ryan Browne scrambled, Zion Elee spun him around, with Sidney Stewart delivering the leveling hit as time expired. The Terps held on to beat the Boilermakers, 34-29, for their first Big Ten win in 413 days.

The matchup between teams that each have just two Big Ten wins over the last three seasons looked the part early, with the Terps and the Boilermakers combining for 69 first-quarter yards.

Purdue got on the board first, kicking a field goal on a short drive after Bryce McFerson's punt went just 27 yards.

To start the second quarter, Maryland's linebackers lost wide receiver Asaad Waseem on a crossing route, and he peeled away for a 37-yard reception that set up another field goal.

Meanwhile, thanks to a Michael Hershey hands-in-the-face penalty that stalled out a promising drive, the Terps' first 16 offensive plays netted them 40 yards.

Maryland finally got past midfield with seven minutes to go in the first half, but that was because of an excellent kick return by Ricardo Cooper Jr.

After that special teams spark, the Terps' offense needed just three plays to reach the end zone. Malik Washington found Chris Durr Jr. in stride for a 31-yard gain before running in a 15-yard score off an option read.

Fortunately for the Terps, that touchdown cut the lead to two points. Maryland's defense bent to the tune of 156 second-quarter yards, but it refused to break, holding the Boilermakers to field goals on each of their first three red zone drives.

After another Purdue field goal, Maryland's two-minute drive was cut short by an incomprehensible interception — Washington's pass hit Dorian Fleming's ready hands and flew into the air for an easy pick.

Purdue couldn't capitalize, though. Elee sacked the quarterback on a crucial third down, pushing the Boilermakers back into a Hail Mary — where the freshman got home again to erase the turnover.

Following the half, Maryland had four straight touchdowns, finding the scoring groove that had evaded it all season.

The Terps' offense earned its first second-half score, grinding over midfield before Na'eem Abdul-Rahim Gladding burst free from a crowded set for a 44-yard score. The second came from a piece of defensive fortune.

Lavain Scruggs got into the backfield and stripped quarterback Ryan Browne, with the Terps recovering on the two-yard line. But on three tries, the run game struck out.

Washington, rushed back onto the field with an injured knee, took matters into his own hands. Receiving the fourth-down snap under center, Washington rose up, cresting over his offensive line to reach the ball into the end zone.

Purdue got a touchdown back, courtesy of some big plays that moved the chains. But DeJuan Williams responded with an even bigger play, running 75 yards untouched into the end zone on the offense's first snap back on the field.

Maryland's defense again held strong in the red zone, forcing the Boilermakers to kick a field goal after having first-and-goal three yards out.

Purdue almost immediately paid for coming short. Cooper scampered away on another kickoff, this time reaching the end zone. However, a block in the back by Jayden Kitchens nullified the score, bringing Maryland back to the 12-yard line.

Durr, who had cooled off through October after a fiery start to the season, had a piece of individual brilliance to give the Terps just enough cushion. Catching a screen deep in the left flat, the Wyoming transfer sliced through the entire defense, climbing the ladder to the right sideline and sprinting to the end zone for an 87-yard score.

Purdue cut the score with a 13-play, 75-yard drive, and it fended off the Terps' offense around midfield to earn one more possession. Ultimately, though, Maryland's red zone defense came out on top.

1. Backfield pressure wins the game. The Terps finished Saturday's game with seven sacks, their most since 2020, and a season-high 13 total tackles for loss. Alongside Elee and his 2.5 sacks, Nahsir Taylor, Trey Reddick and CJ Smith each had multiple tackles for loss.

2. Punting battle lost. McFerson has struggled in 2026 — the preseason Ray Guy watch list punter's 42.21 yard per punt average entering Saturday was second-worst in the Big Ten. With Maryland needing to scrap for field position against the Boilermakers, McFerson's first two punts went for a combined 62 yards. But the senior finally had a short punt go his way, pinning Purdue at the 5-yard line for its final drive.

3. Terps lost their tempers. Five plays into the game, embattled cornerback Dontay Joyner was ejected. Referees determined he threw a punch; three plays earlier, he had also thrown a slap at an opponent. Joyner's was one of nine Maryland penalties on the afternoon.

Emotions remained at a simmer throughout. Messiah Delhomme, DD Holmes and Elee scuffled along the Boilermakers' sideline in the third quarter; only Elee escaped without a personal foul, but none were ejected. The trio continued to make plays to seal the game.

#2775. Arch Manning, Texas football saved by strange fumble call against Missouri

Texas football appeared to catch a break late in the third quarter of its latest SEC game.

The Longhorns trailed Missouri 20-13 at Memorial Stadium in Columbia, Missouri, and faced a third-and-10 at the Missouri 39-yard line. Quarterback Arch Manning's arm was hit on what looked to be an attempted pass, which fell to the ground roughly 20 yards downfield. But the play wasn't ruled an incompletion when the ball hit the ground. Referees didn't blow their whistle, and Manning scampered to pick up what was ultimately deemed a fumble recovered by the offense.

Replay review ensued. The call on the field was upheld, and boos reigned down in a combination of frustration and confusion from the Missouri crowd. Manning added to their frustration three plays later with a 25-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Jermaine Bishop to tie the game at 20-20.

Texas caught a break on its recovered fumble. It was on the unfortunate side of a different officiating decision in the second quarter. Texas appeared to rip the ball from Missouri wide receiver Cayden Lee as he fought for a first-down near the Missouri 35-yard line. But a turnover did not ensue, as officials ruled they awarded Lee forward progress and blew the play dead before the ball was taken from his hands.

Both Texas and Missouri entered Saturday at 6-2, 3-2 SEC. Saturday marks Texas' second true road game this season after Texas' 20-17 win at Tennessee in September.

#2773. Alexander Ovechkin announces this will be his last NHL season: 'Let's have fun'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Alex Ovechkin's 22nd NHL season will be his last, the Washington Capitals superstar announced on Monday."This is gonna be my last year," Ovechkin told his teammates in a video the Capitals posted to social media. "It's sad, but it is what it is. We have an unbelievable team this year. There are 82 games left. Let's make the playoffs, and let's have fun."

Ovechkin has already established himself as the greatest goal-scorer in hockey history with 929 tallies, and he still has 82 games to add to that total before he hangs up his skates.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NHL Draft, Ovechkin immediately established himself as a prolific scorer by notching 52 goals en route to winning the Calder Trophy as a rookie.

Since then, Ovechkin has won the Rocket Richard Trophy as the NHL's leading goal-scorer a record nine times. The Capitals legend's resume also features an Art Ross Trophy and three Hart Trophy wins.

The crowning achievement in Ovechkin's illustrious career is leading Washington to its first Stanley Cup in 2017-18. After coming up short in a number of postseasons prior to that, Ovechkin led all playoff performers with 15 goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as a result.

Following the 2025-26 season, there was speculation that Ovechkin could retire, but he signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Caps.Sensing that this could be Ovechkin's final season, the Capitals loaded up to give their franchise icon one more shot at the Stanley Cup. Washington signed former Buffalo Sabres winger Alex Tuch in free agency and acquired winger Jordan Kyrou from the St. Louis Blues via trade.

No team is as loaded on the wings as the Capitals, and they have one of the best rosters in the Metro Division. Washington has the ingredients to challenge the defending Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and get Ovechkin one more ring before he rides off into the sunset.

#2770. Trent Alexander-Arnold watches from the bench as Fede Valverde scores a stunner from right-back for Real Madrid

Trent Alexander-Arnold joined Real Madrid to become their first-choice right-back, but under Jose Mourinho he is now watching a midfielder do that job instead. Captain Fede Valverde started there again at Mestalla and smashed in the opener against Valencia, while Alexander-Arnold and summer signing Denzel Dumfries were left out of the starting XI once again.

Valverde lined up at right-back for Real Madrid's trip to Valencia on Saturday, with neither Alexander-Arnold nor Dumfries in Mourinho's starting XI. The Uruguayan made the call look inspired in the 28th minute, when Kylian Mbappe's free-kick was blocked by the wall and the ball rolled back to the Real Madrid captain.

Valverde controlled the ball around 20 metres out and drilled a powerful low strike into the net. Arda Guler doubled the lead eight minutes later, and the visitors went in at the break 2-0 up.

Valverde's display was about far more than his goal. According to Sofascore, he had 32 touches in the first half, completed 26 of his 29 passes and was not dribbled past once, while Real Madrid enjoyed 75 per cent of possession.

It was the latest sign that Mourinho's experiment has become a settled plan. Valverde was first moved to right-back during the 1-0 win over Villarreal last month and has since started there against Sevilla, RB Leipzig and Barcelona, as well as at Mestalla.

The shift has hit Alexander-Arnold hardest. The England international has played just 435 minutes in all competitions this season, with only four starts in La Liga, and he was an unused substitute in Real Madrid's last three Champions League games.

His only start since the Villarreal game came in the 3-0 win at Racing Santander, when Valverde missed out with muscular discomfort. It is a sharp fall for a player who made 30 appearances last season despite a string of injuries, while Dumfries has also lost his place only months after arriving.

Real Madrid had won seven games in a row in all competitions before kick-off, so Mourinho has little reason to change a winning side. Speaking at his press conference before the Racing game, he insisted: "In the end, everyone will play."

Alexander-Arnold can count on England. Thomas Tuchel left him out of his World Cup squad but has since recalled him, and he played 90 minutes in both wins over the Czech Republic during the last international break. England face Croatia on Thursday.

#2769. Stats Rundown: 5 numbers from the Mavericks 112-100 Emirates Cup win over the Jazz

The Dallas Mavericks were in a funk for their past two games, with Kyrie Irving sitting one and Cooper Flagg having arguably the worst two-game stretch of his young career. Emirates Cup action raised the intensity and the Mavs stepped up to the tune of a 112-100 win Friday night.

For what felt like the first time in a long time, the Mavs dominated on the boards to the tune of +18 for the night. Dallas knew this was something they needed to work on and they answered the call Friday night. The cherry on top was that rookie Morez Johnson, Jr. led all players 17 boards!

All of those rebounds led to plenty of points for Dallas. They made the most of ending Utah possessions and extending their own possessions, outscoring the Jazz by 15 in second chance points.

The Mavericks got themselves to the line early and often, allowing them to keep the game tight in the first half. Utah was more efficient from the line, missing only a single attempt, but Dallas' 80.6% (25-of-31) was more than enough of an edge, giving the Mavs a +12 advantage from the charity stripe.

The game had an inordinate number of traveling calls; nine to be exact. In the flow of the game, it was quite noticeable and somewhat bizarre. The travel-happy referees were equal opportunity penalizers, handing Utah five of the infractions, and Dallas four of their own.

Dallas opened up a tight game in the third quarter and early part of the fourth. Reeling off a 28-6 scoring run, Dallas extended a one possession game to a 20-point lead. Utah responded with a couple of three-point makes and a smaller run of their own, but that 28-6 run proved to be the deciding factor in a Mavericks' win.

The Mavs needed a win to wash away a bit of the stink from the prior two games and they did all the little things to make it happen against the Jazz. Dallas was locked in on the boards, got to the line, and put together a nice run to build a cushion that proved insurmountable for the Jazz.

We're officially into Week 9 of the NFL season (and the looming NFL trade deadline), where teams will have to make a decision on the intended course of the remainder of their season — are they going all in? Or is it time to tear it all down and look toward the future?

NFL fans also await news on the fate of star running back Jonathan Taylor, who has been touted as a potential trade-deadline mover as the Indianapolis Colts kicked off their franchise reset with a fire sale. They've already traded away two foundational players, Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, for several draft picks as they look to the future, leaving us to wonder whether Taylor could be next.

The Los Angeles Rams could be a deadline buyer, as they've won back-to-back games and are already getting a long-awaited midseason reinforcement in the form of edge rusher Myles Garrett, a two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year and the league's single-season sack record holder.

Garrett's in line for a return to game action on the road Sunday against the Washington Commanders. Coming back from early-season knee surgery that landed him on injured reserve, Garrett has practiced all week.

Shedeur Sanders will start at quarterback for the Cleveland Browns in Week 9 against the New Orleans Saints, head coach Todd Monken announced.

Deshaun Watson returned to practice in a limited capacity on Friday, but remains in concussion protocol. Monken said it's unclear if Watson will serve as the backup this week, though he will be listed as questionable

The Browns' No. 1 quarterback took a helmet-to-helmet hit during the first quarter of Sunday's loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. Watson missed only four snaps, but later reported experiencing concussion symptoms on Monday night.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more ahead of Week 9.

The Broncos are getting a reinforcement in the passing game.

Denver has activated wide receiver Pat Bryant from injured reserve. Bryant played in the team's first four games before suffering an injury that landed him on IR.

The wideout caught nine of his 12 targets for 133 yards and a touchdown. Bryant is expected to make his return on Sunday against the Panthers.

The Lions will be without linebacker Jack Campbell for at least the team's next four games, as they are adding him to injured reserve.

Campbell was involved in a multi-player tackle in Detroit's game against the Vikings that resulted in him leaving the game on a backboard and being taken to a local hospital.

The Lions haven't given many updates, and the most recent was from Campbell himself, who on Wednesday said that he was still in the hospital recovering. The linebacker said he has "full movement" in his lower body and is making progress on movement in his upper body.

Neither Detroit nor Campbell have given any sort of timeline for when he could return to the field. By being added to IR, Campbell would be first eligible to play again in Week 13, depending on his recovery.

Not only will the New Orleans Saints reportedly welcome rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson into the fold Sunday against the Cleveland Browns, but they also plan on activating left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr., per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.

Banks, last year's No. 9 overall pick, suffered a high ankle sprain in September that required surgery. He hasn't played since Week 2.

The delayed debut of New Orleans Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson is reportedly right around the corner.

According to Jordan Schultz, Tyson will be activated off IR to face the Browns in Week 9. The No. 8 overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft has yet to play due to a hamstring injury.

Shedeur Sanders has already been named as the starter for Week 9. The question now is if Watson, who officially cleared concussion protocol on Saturday, will serve as the backup. If he is unable to, Dillon Gabriel will be QB2.

The Denver Broncos are looking to add a tight end before Tuesday's trade deadline.

Evan Engram has 13 receptions for 136 yards and 1 touchdown, and the team reportedly wants to upgrade.

The Broncos aimed high, checking in on Arizona Cardinals All-Pro Trey McBride, who currently leads the NFL with 66 catches. Understandably, the Cardinals said no, according to ESPN. McBride was signed to a four-year extension last year that made him the highest-paid tight end in the league at the time.

Other tight ends that could be available may include the Philadelphia Eagles' Dallas Goedert, Noah Fant from the New Orleans Saints, the Atlanta Falcons' Austin Hooper and the Dallas Cowboys' Luke Schoonmaker.

Following Baltimore's Thursday night loss to Jacksonville, Henry reiterated that he wants to stay with the Ravens.

"I have not mentioned me going anywhere else," he said. "I'm saying, 'Let's go back to work. Let's try to get better and turn this thing around.'"

The Colts remain interested in moving pieces out as they rebuild. According to Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter, along with discussions involving running back Jonathan Taylor, the team is listening in on suitors for quarterback Daniel Jones.

The Ravens were reportedly a team that call, but that was before they went and acquired Jacoby Brissett this week from the Cardinals.

Jones has a $10.51 million injury guarantee for this season that is fully guaranteed in March 15 if he's still on the Colts' roster. Jones could waive the injury guarantee if he wanted to move on.

When asked what happened to Nelson, Macdonald said the interior o-lineman had something he was dealing with when he arrived.

#2765. Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams Hit With NFL Fines

The Detroit Lions picked up a hard-fought 19-15 victory over the Minnesota Vikings in Week 8, but two of their biggest offensive stars are now paying a price for their actions during the game.

On Saturday, the NFL announced that wide receivers Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams were each fined $11,941 for taunting during Detroit's November 1 victory at Ford Field.

That's a combined $23,882 in fines for the Lions' dynamic receiving duo.

Detroit Lions wide receiver Jameson Williams (1) reacts to a penalty after a first down celebration against Minnesota Vikings during the first half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

According to the NFL's official accountability report, both violations occurred during the first quarter.

Amon-Ra St. Brown: $11,941 for taunting with 11:25 remaining in the first quarter.

Jameson Williams: $11,941 for taunting with 4:55 remaining in the first quarter.

Williams' penalty came following a 46-yard reception from Jared Goff that moved Detroit deep into Minnesota territory. However, the receiver was flagged after spinning the football near a Vikings defender, costing the Lions 15 yards.

St. Brown was penalized earlier in the quarter after standing over a Minnesota defender following a running play.

Both incidents resulted in unsportsmanlike conduct penalties during the game.

Interestingly, this isn't the first time Williams has found himself dealing with the NFL's disciplinary process this season.

Earlier in the year, Williams was assessed fines totaling $26,867 for taunting and an illegal celebration during Detroit's Week 2 loss to Buffalo.

However, the receiver successfully appealed both fines, resulting in those penalties being rescinded.

Whether Williams or St. Brown will appeal their latest fines remains to be seen.

Despite the penalties, Detroit ultimately got the result it wanted against Minnesota.

As we previously reported following the victory, Williams caught the go-ahead touchdown pass from Goff in the fourth quarter, helping the Lions hand the Vikings their first loss of the season.

The victory also improved Detroit's record to 5-2, with the Lions leaning heavily on a rushing attack that piled up 230 yards.

The NFL has made it clear that taunting violations can carry consequences beyond the field.

For St. Brown and Williams, that lesson now comes with a combined $23,882 price tag, assuming the fines are upheld.

#2763. Luka Doncic is soaring, Lakers are No. 1 in West. His brilliance is leaving mark

He had recently likened Luka Dončić to a supernova. He said you have to pick your poison against him.

So, when asked if he had any superlatives to offer following Dončić's 53-point, five-rebound, five-assist performance in the Lakers' 124-118 win over the Trail Blazers on Friday, Redick stumbled.

When a reporter started asking another question, he interjected.

"I'm going to just sit around, we'll gather one day and come up with more superlatives," Redick added. "So I'll have more words ready. But for now, I don't have any words."

The hyper-prepared Lakers coach was finally ill-prepared for an assignment.

Redick isn't the only person who has been left dumbfounded following Dončić's blazing start to the season in which he's averaging a league-leading 40.1 points, 7.7 rebounds and 7.6 assists.

In Friday's game, Dončić passed Michael Jordan (347) for the most points scored in the firstnine games of a season since the NBA-ABA merger with 361 points.

Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic shoots a free throw during an NBA basketball game against the Portland Trail Blazers in Los Angeles, Friday, Nov. 6, 2026. AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill

It's the most points anyone has scored in the modern NBA since Wilt Chamberlain in 1962-63.

"I'm having a lot of fun," Dončić said. "Obviously playing basketball, it's a lot of fun for me. It's more [fun] when you play like this and when you win games. So, it's been like this my whole life. Basketball was my dream. Playing in the NBA was my dream. Just living my dream."

The 27-year-old face of their franchise is having an MVP-caliber campaign while leading the Lakers to the No. 1 seed in the Western Conference with an 8-2 record.

No one expected the Lakers to be this good.

And no one expected Dončić to soar to the top of the MVP conversation after he hadn't finished in the top two in voting ever in his career.

Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic, left, drives to the basket against Portland Trail Blazers center Robert Williams III on Friday, Nov. 6, 2026, in Los Angeles. AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill

But if the first few weeks of the season have made anything clear, it's that Redick needs to beef up his vocabulary. He needs to get a thesaurus. Dončić is skyrocketing, and he's carrying the Lakers with him.

There were many incredible moments in the Lakers' 16-point come-from-behind win over the Trail Blazers in which they stormed back after shooting 4-for-23 from beyond the arc in the first half, including missing all 15 of their initial attempts from that distance.

There was the buzzer-beating 62-foot shot that Dončić made at the end of the second quarter, a shot he literally banked in from three-quarters of the court.

"Luka can do some things that maybe a handful, if not no one, can do in basketball," Redick said.

Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic, left, shoots over Portland Trail Blazers center Robert Williams III on Friday, Nov. 6, 2026, in Los Angeles. AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill

There was a little mixup after Dončić notched his 11th 50-point performance in his career, surpassing Kareem Abdul-Jabbar for 10th-most such games in NBA history.

It all started because Ziaire Williams couldn't wait to congratulate Dončić.

So much so that Williams decided to interrupt what he thought was Dončić's walk-off television interview with "NBA on Prime" by approaching him from behind, putting his hands on his shoulders and yelling, "Fifty ball."

Austin Reaves was doing the interview. Not Dončić.

"I'm the wrong white person," said Reaves, who had 25 points.

Did Williams seriously confuse his two teammates? "Deadass," he said, flashing a smile in the Lakers' locker room.

"That was very disrespectful to me," Dončić said jokingly of being confused with Reaves, with whom he shares a brotherly bond.

It has been a wild stretch for Dončić, who's shattering records nightly.

He's leaving his coach at a loss for words. He's making shots from outer space. And he's leaving his teammates seeing his face in everyone.

"I feel like that," he said. "But as long as we win, I'm good."

#2760. Ravens' Roquan Smith fined $35,822 for two hits against Bills

Baltimore Ravens linebacker Roquan Smith has been fined a total of $35,822 by the NFL for two separate violations during last Sunday's 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills, including a facemask penalty involving quarterback Josh Allen.

According to NFL Network's Tom Pelissero, Smith received a $17,911 fine for grabbing Allen's facemask and twisting his head during a touchdown run. The veteran linebacker was assessed an additional $17,911 fine for a hit on a defenseless player during another play in the game.

The disciplinary action comes less than a week after Baltimore suffered its third straight loss to Buffalo, a game in which the Ravens struggled defensively and lost quarterbacks Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to injuries.

The most notable incident occurred during Allen's 1-yard touchdown run in the first quarter, when Smith grabbed the Buffalo quarterback's facemask as he attempted to prevent him from reaching the end zone. Video of the play showed Allen's head being turned as Smith made contact with his facemask. The touchdown stood, and the Bills took an early 7-0 lead.

The incident drew criticism after the game, with questions raised about the lack of an on-field penalty. Buffalo coach Joe Brady later addressed the play, acknowledging he hadn't initially seen the contact but expressing concern about the nature of the tackle.

The NFL reviewed the incident during its weekly disciplinary process and determined that Smith's actions warranted a $17,911 fine.

Smith also received a $17,911 fine for a hit on a defenseless player during a separate incident against Buffalo.

The NFL's disciplinary policies prohibit forcible contact against players deemed defenseless under league rules, with fines assessed based on the nature of the violation and applicable disciplinary standards. The two penalties bring Smith's reported fines from the Buffalo game to $35,822.

This isn't the first time Smith has faced discipline for facemask contact this season. The NFL previously fined him $11,941 for grabbing New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough's facemask during a Week 2 matchup.

The repeated violations put more focus on Smith's tackling technique as the Ravens try to correct their defensive problems.
